item.content:encoded:
One thing about Libra season? It's a soirée! Party invitations, romantic dates, and spontaneous nights out on the town are on the agenda, as per usual. While the signs can expect all of the traditional Libra behavior this season, 2026 has a little more drama in store, especially in relationships. Patience is a virtue, especially now. You'll want to be extra prepared for what the cosmos has in store – for the sake of true love.
Between Sept. 22 and Oct. 23, the sun moves through Libra. This brings your friends, social networks, coworkers, and romantic partners to center stage. Venus, the planet governing relationships and romance, already spent a good chunk of time in Libra (AKA the sign it rules). Libra season will see it locked in sultry Scorpio. This energy brings intensity in the bedroom and how you relate to others on a deep, emotional level. Let's get into it.
How Libra Season 2026 Is Spicing Up Your Love Life
So, how is all the cosmic whiplash influenced? Well, you have not one but two overlapping retrogrades: Venus and Mercury. For many, this double-trouble transit is shaking up relationship dynamics, causing you to reflect on your partnerships, big and small. Venus enters retrograde on Oct. 3 in Scorpio, dredging up past relationship patterns and, yes, even exes. Combine that with the dreaded Mercury retrograde, which starts on Oct. 24, and you've got a punch bowl of celestial chaos that pushes toward reopening past relationship wounds.
Some signs are going to feel the tension in their one-on-one partnerships more than others. Libra, Aries, and Scorpio are predicted to have a bit of a rocky (if not confusing) love life this season. Libras are reflecting on the value of love and relationships in their life. For Aries, they're learning a lot about the importance of moving on from old relationship wounds. Scorpios are processing the way they idealize romance and how to have their independence intact.
On the other hand, the signs that are (thankfully) spared by a chaotic love life this season are Capricorn, Aquarius, and Gemini. Capricorn is focused on their career (what's new?) along with maintaining friendship niceties. Aquarius is navigating through major philosophical breakthroughs over romantic endeavors. For Gemini, they're experiencing a more lighthearted love life as they prioritize pleasure and their creative projects.
Your Libra Season 2026 Love Horoscope, Sign by Sign
Libra season is going to be a whirlwind of romantic highs and lows, and you'll want to be extra prepared. Keep reading for your sun sign and ascendant sign for everything you need to know about love right now.
Aries
Aries, you'll be learning the art of letting go during Libra season. The patterns and behavior that were once tolerated are proving to be a problem, regardless of your relationship status. Venus retrograde is about acknowledging your own shortcomings, which may be the only way to progress love further.
This is an especially transformational (if not uncomfortable) period if you're single or going through a breakup. Now's the time to face your shadow self and get to the root of why things ended. Healing isn't the most glamorous thing, but you may find reprieve in channeling pain into art.
Taurus
Taurus, Libra season feels like an ode to structure, balance, and routine. With Venus retrograde, it's also about how your relationship adds value (or distraction) to your daily operations. Pay attention to how enmeshed love is in your routine – for better or worse.
For single Taureans or those going through a breakup, you're finally getting back into the swing of things. Entering an era where you're not ruminating about what went wrong can feel refreshing. But it's also worth acknowledging your own shortcomings and reflecting on how to pour into yourself so that you can show up as your best self in future connections.
Gemini
Take a deep breath, Gemini; romance is looking fruitful during Libra season. It's more about finding beauty in your daily routine and acknowledging how your romantic relationships influence your health and overall well-being. With Venus retrograde, you're learning how to create stronger boundaries and allow your independence to remain intact in a partnership.
If you're single or going through a breakup, finding the joy in the in-between moments of your daily routine is part of the healing process. This period is all about pleasure! Make art, visit a gallery, or pick up a childhood hobby you once loved as you navigate through this transition.
Cancer
Cancer, romance is feeling like a warm cup of coffee on a chilly autumn morning this Libra season. The focus of the good in your relationship is palpable. It's a perfect time to show appreciation to your partner for helping set a solid foundation for you both. Plan romantic gestures to show your lover how grateful you are for them!
Single Cancers and those going through a breakup are finding solace in their solitude, and it's not a bad thing! This period is all about recentering yourself, especially as Venus retrograde transits your area of pleasure. Getting crafty and relishing in hobbies that spark your inner child pushes you forward in your path of healing and growth.
Leo
Libra season is empowering you to speak up for what you want in a relationship, Leo, and there's no holding back! With Venus retrograde happening in your area of home, expect to feel old wounds and negative communication patterns resurface. Now's the time to choose your battles and differentiate between regressing to past patterns and reclaiming your needs in love.
If you're single or going through a breakup, leaning on your family is more important now than ever. Revisiting your family structures and reflecting on how your upbringing affects your relationship can help build a strong foundation for future relationships. But it can also heal your younger self from the silent suffering you may be experiencing today, too.
Virgo
Virgo, you have a sharp tongue and aren't afraid to use it. During Libra season, though, you're being shown just how not having a filter and being overly judgmental can severely impact your relationship. Venus retrograde is asking you to revisit the way you communicate your needs. Are you replying for the sake of the relationship, or out of bruised self-esteem?
For single Virgos or those going through a breakup, this is a period of rebuilding confidence. Take this time to revisit all the ways your past relationships have impacted how you see yourself. Engage in experiences and hobbies that make you feel secure in who you are and what you bring in relationships.
Libra
There's a lot of pressure to be seen right now, Libra. Your birthday season is bringing attention to what you value in matters of love. It's all about deciding what routines, patterns, and conflicts in a partnership are worth working through and what's no longer tolerable. How is your love life affecting the way you see yourself?
Single Libras, or those going through a breakup, are having a tough time taking things personally, especially during Venus retrograde. It's important to understand the distinction between where you went wrong and incompatibility. Rather than internalize, reflect on misaligned values; separation is often for the best!
Scorpio
Feeling disillusioned lately, Scorpio? Libra season asks you to address deep-seated fears and desires in your relationships. With Venus retrograde happening in your home sign, it's bringing all the darkness of love into the light: insecurity, jealousy, and distrust. People fall short sometimes, but some connections aren't worth being let down constantly.
Inconvenient and possibly hurtful truths about a previous relationship may surface for Scorpios who are single or going through a breakup. Before you prescribe any connection as one big lie, think about the red flags you may have missed and patterns of idealization. Accountability can help you work through the loss.
Sagittarius
Sagittarius, your optimism is one of your stronger traits. But Libra season is getting you to acknowledge the things you look past in your partner, but shouldn't. This isn't to say that your perception of your lover isn't real, but it's worth revisiting your expectations, especially during Venus retrograde. If you get stuck between reality and illusion, use your friendships as a frame of reference.
Single Sagittarians and those going through a breakup are really leaning into the power of friendships. Spending time with friends is a long-understood remedy for a broken heart. Avoid hunting for a relationship simply from desire and instead look for camaraderie in your romantic prospects.
Capricorn
Capricorn, Libra season is emphasizing how your friendships play into your external success. The partnership you're in has more to say about you than you think. Venus retrograde is teaching you the importance of keeping certain details private. Loving out loud is lovely, but it might be impacting the relationship in ways you didn't see coming.
For single Capricorns and those going through a breakup, leaning on friendships becomes a source of power and confidence. This season is about acknowledging the differences between how you move through romantic partnerships and within your friendships. Pay extra attention to your partnered friends and don't be too proud to ask them for guidance on nurturing a connection.
Aquarius
Ideologies are shifting for you during Libra season, Aquarius, and this period is about keeping love low-key. Endurance in a relationship is special. But Venus retrograde is pushing you to learn that not all long-term connections are worth keeping around, especially when you feel like you've outgrown them.
Aquarius folks who are single or going through a breakup see the world of relationships as a totally different place, and in many ways it is! What you previously hypothesized about relationships – dynamics, how it influences status, and affects your career – is quickly changing, especially during Venus retrograde. Reflect on these changes and incorporate how to apply this new wisdom in future relationships.
Pisces
Pisces, Libra season is bringing uncomfortable truths and transformation to your relationships. Thinking about love logically can earn some wisdom in how you operate in relationships. But remember that self-help books and documentaries about relationships can't help you in the feelings department.
If you're single or going through a breakup, the entire concept of intimacy is likely changing. The loss or lack of a partner is making you rethink how you open up emotionally with your romantic prospects. Sometimes it's better to choose wisely before you give others your all. Sex doesn't have to be a sacred or casual thing; it just needs to feel right in your body.

item.content:encoded:
Each sign of the zodiac has its own set of traits that help to define their personalities and set them apart from each other. Wouldn't it be nice to know what the universe has planned for you at the beginning of the day? Keep reading to find out if today will be lucky for you.
ARIES
Don’t minimize your feelings just so others would stay; you are not unpleasant, you are honest. Be honest about what isn’t working in the relationship and provide a tiny step to take today. If you’re single, don’t alter yourself to seem easy-going. Pick someone who can handle serious talk and real plans. Messages should be very long, not clear. Gather someplace you can feel secure and heard. Your heart does not need limitations, it needs freedom. Stand up and say it like it is.
Taurus
Stay true so you can meet who you deserve. Just indicate what you want, how long you have, and what speed you like. If you’re in a relationship, be honest about how you’re feeling and don’t put on a grin to mask your tension. If single, don’t emulate someone to impress. Keep your dress, tone and plan straight forward and straightforward. We can have a short chat in the evening to clear up doubts.
Where you are is the genuine thing. Pretense vanishes, genuineness remains.
GEMINI
Being single is a choice you make. Mentally you crave diversity, but your heart is begging for logic. If you’re committed, ask for interactions that go beyond small talk. If single pick just one that feels firm and curious. Update your profile or first text to show your genuine interests and don’t spread inquiries. And find a place to talk all nite, without a worry in the world. The norms you set are for the protection of your tranquility.
CANCER
Tell me your genuine goal, your wants and your vulnerabilities without apology. If married, divide chores equitably and ask others to give you a break when you are exhausted. If single, avoid dates that require you to do all the planning. Make your responses timely and to the point. Find a quiet place to talk softly. A promise kept will mean so much more than empty promises. Love grows out of being authentic. Already you are valued.
LEO
The one who really gets you will meet you whole not half. Don't let drama suck the shine out of you. Ask for their presence, for praise, for follow-through. If dedicated ... Listen to who in the free world really praises you. Make one firm plan and adhere to it, time after time and location after place. Give cues and watch acts, not clamor. By sundown, you'll know who's solidly behind you. Your daring is a remedy for love.
VIRGO
Trust is the hidden foundation of love. Care for it. Make tiny commitments and keep them over and over. If committed, choose one daily check-in and one weekly goal. If you are single, look for someone who expects quick responses and puts effort into the connection. Don’t overfix it. Keep the date simple. Clearly and simply state your limits and needs. He who demonstrates well signifies more than words. Trust can unfasten the rigorous orderly heart.
LIBRA
Your delight will never dim, no matter how much it shines. Share plans that are casual and only marginally amusing for either party if committed. If you're single, go for folks who like your style, not those who will criticize it. Keep your texts balanced, avoid confusion. Get together somewhere with lots of music and conversation. Just be you. By nite you shall know who adds to your happiness. Real connection will assist your natural illumination, not dim it.
SCORPIO
Don’t mix an appeal from your heart with a call to alignment. Missing someone isn't indication that you and that person are a match. If it is committed, ask yourself if the behavior in the daily mile is supporting trust or not. If single, clear out the muddled signals quickly and look closely at who provides you a promise of action. Keep your plans brief and confidential. Ask a specific inquiry and take the answer; a friend's frank judgment can aid in recognizing the trend.
Sagittarius
Dare to be recognized, not just seen. Allow yourself to be seen as you are, with your ideas, your habit, your restrictions. If you commit, share one actual hope and set a date to work on it. If you’re single, go with a straight text instead of a cool phrase. Clubs, restaurants, pubs, or any open venue where you two can chat without any limitations. Stick to the schedule and leave on time. Your blatant unmasking demands a serious reply.
CAPRICORN
Let love feed, not deplete. You give so much. What do you get? If you choose to commit, develop frequent methods to check in with one another and plan. If you are single, choose relationships that honor your time, money and energy. Make it easy to understand. Say what you want in the simplest words you can find and see what the answer will be. And that tiny supportive action on your part will say it everything. When caring is reciprocal, the less you labor, the more you feel.
Aquarius
You deserve a connection that leaves you with no questions.” If committed, ask your partner: How often do you speak? How do you handle conflict? If single, ask for a plan that includes time and place first, and don’t make vague commitments. Don't be trapped in lateness and half-baked schemes Keep responses timely and to the point. Just put a personal thought out there and see who answers with active listening. Choose a quiet café to avoid distraction. Clarity at sunset enhances mood and seals actual intention.
PISCES
If you have to beg for it, it’s not love. Ask once. Stop asking. Believe the answer. If you’ve committed, ask for one helpful action today and track whether there’s a follow-up. If single, give up pursuing late replies and half-assed plans. Select a setting that favors a peaceful conversation. • Keep your message brief and clear. Drawing a line will help you feel a little more uplifted. You are tender-hearted but you can hold to your values with sternness.
This article is written by, Sidhharrth S Kumaar, Registered Pharmacist, Astro Numerologist, Life & Relationship Coach, Vaastu Expert, IKS Expert, I Ching Expert, Energy Healer, Music Therapist, Author of “Think like a Sage Lead like a CEO” series and Chief Astro Strategy Officer (CASO), NumroVani.

The Libra Sun opposes retrograde Neptune in Aries on Friday, bringing a harsh reality check in your romantic life. You can't keep living in a fantas
item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Friday, September 25: Get Ready For A Reality Check
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for September 25, 2026. The Libra Sun opposes retrograde Neptune in Aries on Friday, bringing a harsh reality check in your romantic life.
While the Libra Sun seeks harmony and compromise, retrograde Neptune in Aries is divulging what you’ve been avoiding. Be mindful of creating a story in your head instead of honoring what is real. You can't keep living in a fantasy. Be ready to accept the truth no matter how difficult it feels, as it is necessary to move forward and find the love meant for you.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Friday, September 25, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be gentle with yourself, Aries. You may have been investing in a relationship that was never going to go where you needed it to. You shouldn't have to sacrifice your desire for commitment or for sharing a home.
Someone can be a good person and still not be a good fit for you. While you’ve glossed over this truth before, on Friday, it's impossible to ignore. You will need to take action because of it.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t talk yourself into love, Taurus. You also can't control what your heart feels or what you need from a relationship.
Just because you can create what you think is best for you doesn’t mean it will actually feel how you hope. Friday is about honoring just that. You can’t talk yourself into love, no matter how much logical sense it makes.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It’s not your job to convince anyone that what you’re doing is right, Gemini. On Friday, you may find yourself defending your relationship or choices to someone you care about.
This isn’t about convincing the other person of the truth. Instead, reflect on why you are so quick to take on this role. In a healthy relationship, you don't need to defend your partner, so be mindful when this arises, as it may be the clarity you need.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It’s OK to question everything, Cancer. While trust is an important part of any relationship, that doesn’t mean you should blindly do so.
Take a step back on Friday and reflect on how well your partner has honored their word. It's possible you're being love-bombed or gaslit by someone who doesn’t actually have any intention of ever committing to you.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Things don’t just happen, Leo. They’re chosen. The universe is always on your side, but that doesn’t mean your fate happens in spite of your choices. Each decision you make or don’t make creates the life you live, including your relationship.
You’ve had an immense amount of faith in the universe as of late, which is good, but the decisions you’re making aren’t in alignment with that. Pay attention to what comes up on Friday and choose to do better.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You should never fear the truth, Virgo. If you’ve found yourself running from the reality of your relationship or hoping it will sort itself out, Friday may feel challenging.
Something is coming to light on September 25, perhaps concerning a third party or your partner's preferences. While you’ve had your suspicions, you can’t ignore what is finally revealed. Trust that it is happening for your greatest good.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Take a step back, Libra. On Friday, try to see your relationship through an outside perspective. You are emotionally attached, and that may be all that has kept you in this connection.
If your best friend were in this relationship, reflect on what you would say to her. There is something hidden you are meant to see, and once you do, your decision will be easy.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Do what will help you live the life you dream of, Scorpio. This might have to do with where you live or the work you do. It could also relate to who you're dating.
While you are in an experimental period, you must be sure you’re not getting too far off course. Take a moment on Friday to reflect so you can be sure where you are now is leading to where you hope to be in the future.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Take accountability for your choices, Sagittarius. On Friday, a friend points out how you’ve been treating your partner or showing up for the dating process. While your first inclination may be to dismiss them, it's better to hold space for what they say.
You are deeply disillusioned about something having to do with your long-term ideals for romance. The conversation you have with this friend helps you take accountability and make better choices.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t expect your personal life to run on autopilot, Capricorn. While you are work-driven, you don't usually invest as much time and energy into your romantic life. Yet that can lead to your partner feeling taken for granted or ignored.
On Friday, acknowledge how your choices have affected the person you love. Be willing to create a healthier balance in your life.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Challenge yourself, Aquarius. You have to be willing to admit when you’re wrong. You have believed you were becoming your most authentic self, yet Friday brings a sudden awareness that you haven’t.
You’ve been making decisions based on someone influential in your life as a child or young adult. But now is your chance to reclaim your truth and the dreams you have for the future.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Never accept less again, Pisces. You are constantly in a state of becoming. So, as much as you’ve learned what you are worth, on Friday you see how you’ve still been settling for less.
Let this awareness help you shift your boundaries and what you believe in for the future. You are in an era of abundance and romance, so start acting like it.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Yankees’ Boone addresses discrepancy over Aaron Judge’s ‘moderate’ calf strain: ‘We’re all in this together’
item.dc:creator: Peter Sblendorio
item.description: After a discrepancy in comments involving Aaron Judge’s calf injury, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Thursday that “we’re all in this together.” Judge took issue Wednesday night with Boone characterizing the slugger’s calf strain as having a “moderate” grade. “We’ve talked a little bit about it,” Boone said before Thursday night’s series finale against the Tampa Bay Rays in the Bronx. “I don’t want to get too much into that, but at the end of the day, we’re all in this together, and in his case
item.content:encoded:
After a discrepancy in comments involving Aaron Judge’s calf injury, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Thursday that “we’re all in this together.”
Judge took issue Wednesday night with Boone characterizing the slugger’s calf strain as having a “moderate” grade.
“We’ve talked a little bit about it,” Boone said before Thursday night’s series finale against the Tampa Bay Rays in the Bronx.
“I don’t want to get too much into that, but at the end of the day, we’re all in this together, and in his case, trying to get him right and get him healthy so he can be an option for us here at some point. We’re also going to listen to the injury. I see it as just a passionate player that’s doing all he can to get back for his teammates.”
Judge landed on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a right calf strain, putting his playoff status in question.
While the Yankees have not disclosed the grade of the strain, Boone on Tuesday said it was “moderate.” Boone also said that day that he was “not expecting” Judge to be back for the Yankees’ Wild Card playoff series, which begins Tuesday, but didn’t rule anything out.
Judge, meanwhile, reiterated Wednesday night that he hopes to return in time for next week’s postseason opener.
“Everybody’s ‘moderate’ is a little different,” Judge said. “I think your moderate is a little different than my moderate, and so on and so on. So I don’t know why [Boone] used those words, but I’m trying to come back as soon as I can.”
Broadly, the Boston Sports Medicine & Research Institute considers a moderate calf strain to be of the second-degree and says that grade of injury typically requires three to six weeks of rest and recovery. Judge suffered the injury on Sept. 16.
The Yankees have not disclosed a timeline for Judge, who had returned on Sept. 8 after missing the previous 84 games due to a fractured rib.
“The bottom line is Aaron and I have always had an amazing relationship, and still do, and will,” Boone said. “This is about a player that is pouring everything he possibly can into being ready, and we’re gonna support that. When he’s ready, we’ll make a call of when that is, based on how he’s doing. It’s Thursday today. We may not make that call until Tuesday morning.”
Judge shared a similar sentiment Wednesday, calling Boone “my guy” and saying the manager “makes the right decisions.”
“My goal is to come back as soon as I can,” Judge said. “That’s what we’re doing right now. So if [Boone] says I’m not going to be ready, I got no control over that. I got control over what I can do to try to get back as soon as I can.”
Judge — a three-time American League MVP, including in 2024 and 2025 — is hitting .241 with 18 home runs, 41 RBI and an .871 OPS in 66 games this season.
The 34-year-old Judge received a Platelet-Poor Plasma (PPP) injection in his calf on Monday. Judge has not resumed hitting, Boone said Thursday.
“He’s doing all the things in the training room, all the modalities that he can take advantage of,” Boone said. “He’s moving on the treadmill, things like that, doing the different exercises to get that calf healed.”

Love Horoscope Today, September 25, 2026: Today’s love energy calls for calmness, patience, and honest communication to avoid emotional turmoil and misunderstandings. Several signs, including Aries, Cancer, and Aquarius, are encouraged to openly express feelings of distrust or coldness and resolve hidden grievances before they escalate. Leo and Pisces are advised to avoid jealousy and quick tempers to maintain harmony. Libra plays the important role of mediator, helping to restore peace where tensions have arisen. Sagittarius benefits from listening carefully to their partner’s feelings, and Capricorn is reminded to stay calm and sensitive and to resist the urge to walk away in frustration.

Ganesha says you are feeling somewhat emotional today and suffering from a sense of mistrust towards your partner. You may even feel that their loyalty is in question. When tough issues come up in your relationship today, you may want to bury your head in the sand so that you don’t get caught up in any unnecessary drama. It’s okay to stay away from arguments, but make sure you address your concerns.

Ganesha says you should be careful about what words come out of your mouth today and make sure they are not harsher than necessary. You may feel like you are only being honest, but you can rest assured that your loved one will not see it the same way. Be gentle and control your temper today. This will save you from problems in the long run.

Ganesha says that there may be troubles in your love life today, and you should not upset your partner in any way. Make sure that you are not engaging in any manipulative or spiteful behavior by blaming your partner for some of your past indiscretions. Flirting with someone else in front of your partner will only create animosity between you and ultimately make both of you unhappy. If you have issues that need to be discussed, talk about them openly and decide together how to heal your wounds.

Ganesha says, try to focus on building trust and communication in your romantic relationship with your partner today. Your partnership will suffer if there is a lack of trust, and you are currently headed down that path. Make sure you take out time to have a face-to-face conversation with your loved one today and clear any grievances that may have arisen quietly and secretly.
Leo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says try to avoid jealousy in your relationship today, as it can create a rift between you and your partner. Neither be jealous of your partner’s friends nor give your partner any reason to be jealous of you. There is no place for jealousy in a healthy romantic relationship. It is better to talk about this with complete honesty and openness.
Virgo Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that today you may feel a little sad due to recent arguments and misunderstandings in your love life. However, ignore it, as these frustrating periods are fleeting. Your job is to keep a cool head and not start arguments that will only bring misery to you and your partner. Express yourself calmly and clearly, and your partner will listen to you.
Libra Love Horoscope Today
Ganesha says that in the world of romance, today you will play the role of a peacemaker. For some reason, some tension has arisen in your home or in your relationship, and it seems that only you can resolve the matter. Be diplomatic and objective in your approach, and the situation should return to normal soon. If you need to be away from your partner for a while, take time off.

Ganesha says that today, you will find yourself getting into petty fights with your partner without even realizing how it keeps happening. At least today, make sure you are focusing on the issue at hand and not blindly attacking your partner. This will destroy an otherwise healthy relationship and sow the seeds of anger and resentment. Use your language skills to clear up misunderstandings today.

Ganesha says that on the romantic front, you need to focus on listening to your partner today, as things are likely to get a little tense. He or she is trying to tell you something, but you are not willing to listen. Sit in a quiet place without distractions and let your partner tell you how they feel. Spending this time together will benefit your relationship and ultimately strengthen your bond.

Ganesha says that today, you should stay calm in your relationship, as there is a possibility of you walking away from your relationship without any reason. Make sure that you are sensitive to your partner’s needs. Your angry temper is only a temporary situation, so try to wait it out and stay calm. You’re getting stressed will not help your relationship, and your partner may feel somewhat resentful of your behavior.

Ganesha says that today, you may feel that you are not getting along with your romantic partner, and your relationship has become cold. You may feel like they are judging you or suspecting you of something you have not done. Even if your partner has not said anything, take it upon yourself to talk to him or her to clarify the situation. It may be awkward at first, but you will find that it helps get your relationship back on track, and you will feel better in the end.
Pisces Love Horoscope Today

Married couples may find themselves embroiled in unnecessary arguments and arguments. This can be avoided if you show a little sensitivity towards your partner’s needs. Try to stay calm and sensible at this time.
Quick Answers
Aries feels emotional and experiences a sense of mistrust toward their partner, needing to address concerns without drama. item.title: [hottytoddy.com] The sweetest revenge is forgetting Lane Kiffin matters - HottyToddy.com - Ole Miss Sports, Oxford Entertainment, Dining & More
item.dc:creator: Taylor Hodges
item.description: Lane Kiffin’s departure from Ole Miss has always been described as a breakup. One person leaves for someone else, and the other is left angry or depressed or both. The resentment builds fast, and there’s that instinct to get revenge. In relationships, revenge can look like anything. New car. New clothes. Better job. item.content:encoded:
Lane Kiffin’s departure from Ole Miss has always been described as a breakup. One person leaves for someone else, and the other is left angry or depressed or both. The resentment builds fast, and there’s that instinct to get revenge.
In relationships, revenge can look like anything. New car. New clothes. Better job. New partner who makes the old one look like a mistake.
Then you run into each other and get to show you’re better off without them. That’s the moment.
Ole Miss got its moment Saturday night in front of 70,033 people at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. The Rebels beat Kiffin and LSU’s $50 million roster, and it felt like bumping into an ex while wearing designer clothes, driving a Ferrari and sitting next to someone who’s clearly an upgrade.
What comes next, though, is usually just as hard as the breakup: moving on.
This column isn’t to say Ole Miss fans should forgive, forget or suddenly wish Kiffin well. It’s OK to hope LSU loses because, well, it’s LSU and that’s what Ole Miss fans do. But there is a difference between remembering something and continuing to live in it.
If fans keep bringing up Kiffin in every social media or message board post, they’re still allowing him to take up an enormous amount of space in Ole Miss football. If everything is framed through Kiffin, does the program ever truly become Pete Golding’s?
“Kiffin never did this,” or “This proves Ole Miss didn’t need Kiffin,” serve no purpose beyond momentary gratification.
Even positive comparisons have the same effect. Ole Miss making the playoffs becomes about Kiffin. Golding winning a big game becomes about Kiffin.
At some point, continuing to define Pete Golding’s Ole Miss program by its relationship to Lane Kiffin does Golding almost as much of a disservice as constantly comparing a new quarterback to the one he replaced.
It can also drown out what Ole Miss is accomplishing on the field.
This is a team with postseason aspirations. There are stars like Trinidad Chambliss, Kewan Lacy, Deuce Alexander, Will Echoles and Suntarine Perkins, along with a head coach who has quickly become one of the most popular figures around the program.
They deserve to be the center of attention more than the coach who chose to leave. Every conversation about what Kiffin tweeted or what LSU did Saturday is a conversation that isn’t about the Ole Miss team actually playing.
And you better believe the players and coaches see the talk. They’ll always say the right thing about not paying attention to that stuff, but they’re human, and there have been times when the conversation is impossible to ignore.
They’re also constantly asked about Kiffin, LSU, how this season compares to last season and how Golding differs from the coach he replaced.
Some of that is unavoidable. After beating then-No. 24 Louisville in the season opener, Chambliss was asked about LSU during a SportsCenter interview. That was two weeks before the Tigers would come to Oxford, and it was just another example of how often Ole Miss is viewed through the lens of LSU and Kiffin.
The more Kiffin remains part of the daily conversation around Ole Miss, the harder it becomes for the people inside the program to completely leave that chapter behind.
Again, this column isn’t about convincing anyone to hope Kiffin wins the rest of LSU’s games this season. The anger over his departure is justified. The 32-24 win over LSU last Saturday provided the outlet for that anger to be unleashed.
But staying obsessed with Kiffin keeps him at the center of Ole Miss football instead of Golding, Chambliss, Lacy and a team with realistic hopes of making the College Football Playoff.
There’s also a selfish reason for fans to move on: Ole Miss football is pretty fun right now.
This team is good. It has stars. It has legitimate postseason goals. If every big win is followed by wondering what Kiffin thinks, then part of the experience is still being defined by someone who left.
At some point, Ole Miss fans should be able to enjoy Ole Miss success simply because it belongs to Ole Miss.
Ultimately, fans are cheating themselves by experiencing the program’s current success primarily through their feelings about somebody who is no longer part of it.
Because the best revenge isn’t making Kiffin watch Ole Miss succeed.
It’s eventually not caring whether he’s watching.

item.content:encoded:
Is moving on really moving too fast?
Stars and fans debate changing attitudes towards the end of marriage
A candid discussion about divorce has turned into one of the latest celebrity debates in Pakistan, after veteran actor Saba Faisal questioned how society now responds to the end of marriages, prompting strong reactions from fellow actors and fans over grief, stigma and women's right to leave difficult relationships.
Faisal made the comments during an appearance on a TV's talk show, where she reflected on what she described as a significant change in social attitudes towards divorce.
"Before, when someone used to get divorced, there used to be a 'Sog' happening for months," Faisal said, referring to the mourning and grief that traditionally followed a divorce within a family. She contrasted that response with what she sees today, saying that divorced women could now casually mention their separation during conversations before moving on with their lives.
"Dads couldn't do anything, but now when we find out girls have got divorced, it's mentioned casually over a phone call," she said, adding that she had travelled abroad afterwards and tried to figure things out.
Her comments quickly spread online, with celebrities and social media users divided over whether the changing response to divorce represents a loss of sensitivity towards marriage or a greater willingness to acknowledge that marriages can end for different reasons.
Actor Hira Khan was among the strongest voices to respond. In an Instagram story, she wrote, "It's better to go through this than to be carried through a grave," before adding, "She needs help."
Khan argued that divorce should not be confused with celebration and highlighted the circumstances that can make leaving a marriage a matter of safety and dignity. "No one celebrates divorce," she wrote, adding that women have a religiously recognised right to seek it.
She also criticised what she described as the policing and shaming of women who choose to leave marriages. "I'm half your age, but I understand this much," Khan wrote. "Perhaps I was raised to understand that a woman's dignity, safety and right to choose matter."
Faisal's daughter, actor Sadia Faisal, subsequently appeared to respond to Khan, writing, "I wish I could see this so-called actress someday."
Actor Zoya Nasir also entered the discussion, writing in the comments, "Oh. My. God. I have SO much to say, with all due respect. What a dangerous and twisted narrative."
Not everyone, however, agreed with the criticism directed at Faisal. Dr Ejaz Waris offered a more conciliatory perspective, agreeing that divorce should not be celebrated while arguing that its emotional impact can extend to both families.
Fans similarly debated whether discussions about divorce had unfairly focused on the woman's family. Some pointed out that the husband's family can also experience grief, while others argued that the depth of that pain is difficult to understand until a divorce involves one's own daughter.
At the same time, some users defended Faisal, saying her central point was simply that divorce had become more normalised and that people could now return to their everyday lives more quickly following a separation.
The controversy comes shortly after Faisal spoke at length in another interview about the way her comments are handled online. She criticised the practice of editing remarks into short clips designed to generate viral reactions.
"The respect and honour we have built over our entire lives gets severely disturbed when a couple of words are spliced together and edited into the video," she said. Calling virality "a strange illness", Faisal said she had begun taking longer breaks from public appearances because of the way apparently ordinary remarks could be repackaged into controversy.
The actor has also previously attracted criticism for her views on marriage and family, making her latest comments part of a broader public discussion around traditional expectations and changing attitudes among younger generations.
At the heart of the latest debate is a distinction that has emerged repeatedly in the reactions: acknowledging divorce as a painful experience does not necessarily mean treating it as something desirable, while reducing stigma does not necessarily erase the grief associated with the end of a marriage.
For some of Faisal's critics, a woman being able to move forward after divorce is a sign of greater acceptance rather than indifference. For those defending her, the actor was drawing attention to what she sees as a decline in the social and familial gravity once attached to the breakdown of a marriage.

item.title: [statesboroherald.com] Who exactly can file a wrongful death lawsuit?
item.dc:creator: Statesboro Herald
item.description: When the unthinkable happens and a loved one is lost due to the negligence or misconduct of another, the right to seek justice falls primarily on the shoulders of immediate family members. item.content:encoded:
When the unthinkable happens and a loved one is lost due to the negligence or misconduct of another, the right to seek justice falls primarily on the shoulders of immediate family members. In the realm of wrongful death claims, spouses, children and parents of unmarried children are often at the forefront, bearing the legal status to act as primary plaintiffs. This hierarchy of claimants is not just a legal formality; it reflects the profound personal and economic losses these individuals suffer.
As the closest relatives, they are presumed to be the most affected by the absence of the deceased, both emotionally and financially, and the law recognizes their need for reparation.
Extended family and financial dependents
But what about the extended family and those who financially depended on the deceased? The rights of siblings, grandparents and even non-relatives who may have been financially reliant on the deceased can vary significantly. While not typically in the front line for claims, these individuals may still have the right to compensation under certain circumstances.
Understanding the nuances of who is entitled to file a wrongful death claim requires a careful examination of the relationship with the deceased and the financial impact of their loss. It's a complex area that underscores the importance of each case's unique details.
State-specific laws and statutes of limitations
Embarking on a wrongful death lawsuit is a journey that is navigated differently in every state. Each state carries its own set of rules and regulations that govern who is eligible to file a claim. This patchwork of laws means that what applies in one jurisdiction may not hold true in another, making local legal counsel not just helpful but essential.
For residents of Bulloch County and surrounding areas, understanding Georgia's specific wrongful death statutes is the first step in assessing the viability of a claim. It's a critical aspect that underscores the importance of consulting with a knowledgeable local attorney who can provide guidance tailored to the state's legal landscape.
Timeframe for filing a claim
Time is of the essence in wrongful death cases, as the law imposes strict deadlines known as statutes of limitations. These legal time limits dictate how long you have to file a claim, and missing this window can mean forfeiting your right to seek justice altogether. In Georgia, the statute of limitations for filing a wrongful death claim typically stands at two years from the date of death. This underscores the urgency of taking legal action promptly.
Proof of relationship and impact
Establishing a claim in a wrongful death lawsuit is not merely a matter of asserting a loss. Claimants must substantiate their relationship to the deceased and demonstrate the tangible impact the loss has had on their lives. This proof goes beyond blood ties; it encompasses the full spectrum of emotional and financial support that the deceased provided. This process may be more straightforward for immediate family members, but for others, it can be a complex legal challenge. The depth of the relationship, the extent of dependency, and the nature of support previously provided are all scrutinized to establish the legitimacy of a claim.
Exceptions and special circumstances
There are, however, exceptions and special circumstances that can alter who has the standing to sue for wrongful death. In some cases, individuals who are not immediate family members may be granted the right to file a claim if they can demonstrate a significant enough impact on their lives due to the death. This might include dependents who are not related by blood but were financially supported by the deceased, or even a life partner with whom there was a cohabitation arrangement. Understanding these exceptions is crucial, as they can open the door for additional claimants who otherwise might not have considered themselves eligible.

If you are grappling with the loss of a loved one due to someone else's negligence and are considering a wrongful death claim, Josh D. Tucker is here to help. We are committed to providing compassionate and effective legal representation to ensure that your rights are upheld and that you receive the compensation you deserve. item.dc:creator: Syeda Khaula Saad
item.description: It’s no secret that everyone is a little tired of dating apps. In 2024, research showed that consistent users of these apps were experiencing burnout symptoms. item.content:encoded:
It’s no secret that everyone is a little tired of dating apps. In 2024, research showed that consistent users of these apps were experiencing burnout symptoms. If you’ve ever spent 30 minutes swiping left on a sea of cringe prompt responses and pictures of men holding fish, you’re not surprised at this. Conversations seem to go nowhere, people feel very brave saying unhinged things to each other through a screen, and everyone is lying about their height.
Throwing in a subscription fee on top of that? No.
We get it: Businesses need to make money. But when a dating app hides its best features—you know, the ones that actually help you get a date—behind a paywall, it makes a user a lot less likely to want to keep swiping.
And while plenty of apps have jumped on this capitalistic train of “selling” love, not all of them have left their users with the scraps of the apps.
There are still some dating apps that are letting users look for love without having to plug in their credit card information. So you’re free (literally) to focus on what’s important: finding someone you think you could tolerate enough to go on a date with IRL.
Facebook Dating
Okay, the idea of still being on Facebook is daunting enough, so I understand the hesitation of dating on it. But as someone who has tried Facebook Dating in the past, I have to say it’s actually a pretty good dating platform. And if you’re worried that it’s just a means of dating people you “friended” in high school, it’s not.
It has a free matching and messaging experience, and if you already have Facebook downloaded you don’t have to worry about adding another app to your phone.
Feeld
If you’re looking for a dating experience outside of the norms of modern-day courting, Feeld is a great (and free) option. It’s for people looking to explore everything from nonmonogamy to casual hookups and other relationship styles. You can create a profile, connect with mutual likes, and chat—all without paying. While there are tiers that require a subscription, those just come with unlimited likes and the option to see who liked you.
Hinge
Okay, Hinge is definitely an app that has some features locked behind a payment but the app still offers a lot of great options for people who don’t want to whip out their credit card. The free version of the app gives you all of the essentials: browsing profiles, sending likes, matching, and chatting with matches. Just keep in mind that there’s a daily like limit (but I’ve never reached it, so you’ll be fine).
Tinder
Tinder is probably going to give you the biggest possible dating pool—and a lot of that access is for free. You can create a profile, like people, match, and message for free. The only thing to note is that using the paid option will give you access to premium prompts and the ability to set certain preferences.
Bumble
All of Bumble’s basic features (including its safety verification ones) are totally free when you download the app. This means you can find matches and—if you identify as a woman—message first all for free. The app lets you have safe, meaningful interactions without having to pay a dime.
OkCupid
If you want more than three photos and some prompts to base your swipe on, OkCupid is a great option. It’s free tier includes compatibility-focused profiles and extensive questions so you’re really getting a good idea of who someone is before you match with them.

item.content:encoded:
Senate clears Blackburn-backed bill requiring dating app fraud alerts
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WZTV) — The U.S. Senate has passed a bipartisan bill backed by Tennessee Sen. Marsha Blackburn that would require dating apps to alert some users when an account that messaged them is banned for suspected financial fraud.
The Senate passed H.R. 2481, known as the Romance Scam Prevention Act, without amendment by unanimous consent on Sept. 23. The House passed the measure in June 2025, meaning the bill now heads to President Donald Trump.
Blackburn, a Republican, introduced Senate companion legislation with Democratic Sen. John Hickenlooper of Colorado. The measure that cleared Congress was introduced in the House by Republican Rep. David Valadao of California.
If signed, the law would take effect one year after enactment.
Under the bill, an online dating service would have to send a fraud-ban notification to a user who received a message from an account that was later banned because the service determined there was a significant risk the account holder would try to fraudulently obtain money.
MORE NEWS | New Tennessee poll shows Blackburn with big lead, Trump's approval underwater
The requirement would not apply to every person who may have interacted with the account. The bill specifically refers to users who received a message from the banned account through the dating service.
The notice would need to identify the banned account and tell the recipient when they most recently sent or received a message with that user. It also would need to warn that the person may have used a false identity or attempted to defraud users, advise people not to send cash or financial information and provide fraud-prevention resources and customer-service contact information.
Dating apps generally would have 24 hours after issuing a fraud ban to send the notice. The bill allows an app to take up to three days in some circumstances and permits longer delays if requested by law enforcement during an active investigation.
RELATED COVERAGE | Man accused of posing as 49ers player in $1.3M romance scam seen in video
The Federal Trade Commission would enforce the law, while state attorneys general and other authorized state consumer-protection officials could bring civil actions.
The legislation focuses on a common way romance scammers try to build trust before seeking money. The FTC reported that nearly 70,000 people reported romance scams in 2022, with reported losses reaching $1.3 billion.
But dating apps are only one route scammers use. Among 2022 romance-scam loss reports that identified a contact method, the FTC said 40% began on social media and 19% began on a website or app.
In Tennessee, the FBI reported that people 60 and older filed 1,577 fraud complaints in 2023 and reported losing about $43.75 million. That was up from about $36.57 million in reported losses in 2022 — an increase of roughly 19.6%.
Those Tennessee figures include all reported fraud types involving people 60 and older, not romance scams alone.
The FTC advises people not to send cash, gift cards, wire transfers or cryptocurrency to someone they know only online. Suspicious profiles or messages can be reported to the dating app and to ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

item.content:encoded:
Matchmaking is having a moment, whether it's an AI matchmaker for college students or human matchmakers with decades of experience. And while singles are increasingly vexed by dating apps, the platforms are trying to pull in loved ones to help them date, too — like with Hinge's recent feature Friend's Take.
Amid these trends, a new app for both singles and wannabe matchmakers launches today: Rivet. Founded by former Tinder and Match Group executive Taru Kapoor, Rivet is a "social matching" app that will attempt to replace algorithms with the wisdom of crowds. Users sign up as Daters or Matchers, and all are encouraged to pair up others.
"Dating has always been social," said Kapoor in a press release shared with Mashable. She spent years thinking that dating apps were removing friction from meeting each other, but instead, "we removed the people."
You May Also Like
AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections
Tinder — top pick for finding hookups
Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups
Dating apps created matches by connecting people who wouldn't have met otherwise, Kapoor continued, but a side effect was that they turned something fundamentally social and human — dating — into a transactional, isolated activity.
"I built Rivet to change that," she said. "Rivet is built on a simple truth: humans understand chemistry and compatibility in a way that no algorithm can. You don't have to find your person entirely on your own, let people help you find your person."
How does Rivet work?
On Rivet, all Daters are also Matchers, but not all Matchers are Daters, Kapoor told Mashable. "Even if you're married, in a relationship or simply not currently looking to date, you can still join Rivet to be a Matcher and help people find meaningful connections," she said over email. You can make a Dater profile later if you'd like, but you're never required to.
Matchers provide their opinions on potential pairs and recommend introductions for users they believe would be a good couple. Pairs who receive high "Social Matching scores" are then introduced to each other on the app, and each person decides whether to match and start a conversation.
You can be on Rivet solely as a Dater, Kapoor continued, though the app encourages Daters to participate in matching others.
More than two-thirds (68 percent) of Gen Z and millennials said they'd be interested in helping someone they don't personally know find a potential romantic match (if they can do so anonymously, and the pair themselves made the final decision), according to a national survey of over 2,000 U.S. adults commissioned by Rivet.
And some prizes can sweeten the deal, too. Matchers can receive rewards for helping people find love, according to Rivet's website. "Match a pair that you think will click or call a mismatch, and you earn Karma. Karma gets you bragging rights and can be redeemed for rewards," it states.
Currently, reaching 15,000 Karma with a strong MQ (Matcher Quotient, the app's way of displaying a Matcher's thoughtfulness and accuracy) can be redeemed for $30 equivalent in cash or gift cards, Kapoor said. The team is working on making more reward and redemption options available soon.
Those with high MQ might also be bestowed as Elite Matchers.
In addition to the app, Rivet also hosts live events, such as a dating show in New York City in early Oct.
More dating apps are adding AI — meaning, more algorithms — and Rivet is bucking the trend. It's now available for free on iOS and Android.
Anna Iovine is the associate editor of features at Mashable. Previously, as the sex and relationships reporter, she covered topics ranging from dating apps to pelvic pain. Before Mashable, Anna was a social editor at VICE and freelanced for publications such as Slate and the Columbia Journalism Review. Follow her on Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
You will feel emotionally distant, think privately and have a stronger need to know what is real. Moon is in Aquarius, and Shatabhisha Nakshatra makes you feel and think free. Single people may prefer meaningful space over constant attention. Couples may notice habits that have quietly undermined trust.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
If the other person needs to be alone, don’t get emotionally close. Shatabhisha can make it hard to express your feelings. But Aquarius is all about freedom. Couples may find relief by relaxing the pressure and concentrating on what is really bothering them. Single people shouldn’t confuse mystery for depth. Still, consistency matters; if communication is fuzzy, wait for more evidence before making a serious emotional decision.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Leo: You feel ignored if someone doesn’t show affection. Don’t ask for proof of interest. Let the other person show care in their own unique way.
Taurus: When the unknowns are present, you might be clinging tighter to what you know works. A relationship can change without becoming unstable. Before you fight it, try to understand what is changing.
Scorpio: You may be more sceptical than yesterday. Don't watch / test / keep an eye on someone.
Trust what you know, not what you think might happen.
Cancer: When someone is quieter, you may feel more emotionally sensitive. Don’t think silence is about you. Maybe they need space for an entirely different reason.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Aquarius: If you value your independence, you might find someone who also likes their personal space. Single people connect through technology, community groups, social causes or shared intellectual interests.
Gemini: You could find yourself having a very odd conversation with someone that could get very personal. Someone can show a side of themselves that makes the connection feel more interesting and stronger.
Libra: If you can keep your cool about your feelings, you'll do well in a tricky romantic situation. Stay cool, and someone might be comfortable enough to talk to you.
Sagittarius: You may be attracted to a different breed. Singles may meet someone they never thought they would, and couples can help each other by giving each other more space.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Aries: You still have feelings for someone. Be careful not to move things along too fast, or they may slow down.
Virgo: Taking a break from constantly analysing a relationship may help you to understand it better.
Capricorn: Even if it means less time together due to practicalities, your love is strong.
Pisces:
Emotional insight is good, but don't let assumptions substitute for actual information.
Lucky Action of the Day
Today, it’s good to give one relationship a little space. If pressure is relieved, then real interest, trust and emotional clarity can come forth naturally.

Mumbai, September 24 (IANS) Politician Raghav Chadha marked 3 years of marital bliss with Bollywood actress Parineeti Chopra with an adorable wish on social media.
Expressing his gratitude for the life the two of them are building together, Raghav uploaded a video montage of some rare moments of the lovebirds together on IG.
He wrote on the photo-sharing app, "Three years and I’m still not sure if I’ve found the words to describe how much you mean to me. Which is saying something, because I’m usually not short of them (sic)."
"From that first breakfast together to now, you have somehow made every version of life feel warmer, fuller and more like home. Particularly, this past year has given us so much to hold close, and somehow made me even more grateful for the life we are building together. Happy anniversary @parineetichopra (sic)," he added.
Raghav concluded the post, saying, "I feel incredibly lucky that I get to do life with you."
Parineeti's mother and Raghav's mother-in-law, Reena Chopra, wished the couple in the comment section, saying, "Awww !! Love you both! Happy Anniversary".
Parineeti and Raghav tied the knot on September 24, 2023, in a private ceremony in Udaipur.
The couple embraced parenthood on October 19, 2025, as they welcomed their son Neer.
These two are frequently seen supporting each other on social media.
Most recently, Raghav praised Parineeti ahead of her OTT debut with 'Shaque'.
Sharing the recently released trailer of 'Shaque' on his official Instagram handle, Raghav penned, “So proud of you @parineetichopra...I know how much you gave to Shaque, especially through a time that was already very special for us. Having spent some time at the shoot in Shimla, I also got to see the warmth and talent of the team behind it. An exceptionally talented bunch, and clearly one you had a lot of fun working with.”

item.title: [vice.com] There's a New Way to Meet Cute Guys, but Does It Actually Work?
item.dc:creator: Sammi Caramela
item.description: The dating world is so bleak right now that some singles are calling restaurants/bars ahead of time to see whether any cute guys are there. And while this is a harmless, silly dating trend, it shows how much daters crave actual meet-cutes. Surely, they can just swipe on an app and find a dinner date that way. item.content:encoded:
The dating world is so bleak right now that some singles are calling restaurants/bars ahead of time to see whether any cute guys are there. And while this is a harmless, silly dating trend, it shows how much daters crave actual meet-cutes. Surely, they can just swipe on an app and find a dinner date that way. But there’s something special about meeting someone out in the real world. You know, the old-fashioned way.
In fact, according to Hily Dating App data, 62% of Gen Z women and 55% of Gen Z men are open to meeting someone IRL. The problem? Well, 38% of women and 42% of men also feel anxious about approaching strangers. Perhaps that is why some call ahead of time, mentally preparing for the dating pool they’re about to dip their toes into for the evening.
Videos by VICE
What Does the Calling-Ahead Trend Reveal About Modern Dating?
According to Dr. Sabrina Romanoff, a relationship expert at Hily Dating App and Harvard-trained clinical psychologist, this trend highlights the tension in modern dating.
“It’s ironic that people are trying to manufacture these impromptu and spontaneous meet-ups while simultaneously trying to control variables like you can with online dating,” says Dr. Sabrina Romanoff. “It speaks to our current desire to have our cake and eat it too.”
Is the Calling-Ahead Trend Actually Beneficial?
Sure, this lighthearted, funny trend could help in dating, as it lets you analyze your options before you even see them. However, if you go into every social outing with the hope to meet someone, you’re likely missing out on genuine connections and chance encounters. Instead of constantly focusing on finding a partner, try being present in every moment, whether grabbing drinks with your friends or having dinner with family.
“I would not recommend this approach because it comes with the mindset that going out, spending time with your girlfriends, and having new experiences are only ‘successful’ if you meet a cute potential new partner,” says Dr. Romanoff. “This inevitably places pressure on dating—it can make you feel more desperate and often leave you feeling worse if you don’t achieve your ‘objective’ at the end of the night.”
Trust me, I know how frustrating it can be to hear the advice of, “Just let love come to you!!!” and “It’ll happen when you least expect it!!!!” So, I won’t tell you either of those statements. They didn’t help me when I was single throughout my 20s, and honestly, they didn’t even prove to be true in my case. I had to actively work on myself and focus on my dating goals to find the right person.
But going to the other extreme of constantly dwelling on your singlehood and obsessing over meeting the love of your life won’t help either. So, sure, if you want to engage in this silly trend of calling a restaurant or bar ahead of time to scope out its patrons, go for it. Just don’t make meeting your person the core goal of every night out.

item.content:encoded:
Nick Cannon is "always open" to getting back together with Mariah Carey.
The Masked Singer host married the Hero hitmaker in 2008 and though they divorced in 2016, he revealed they speak "almost every day" about their 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe and he still regards her as his "greatest friend".
He told Us Weekly magazine: "We talk almost every day or every other day, specifically just about the kids. We were laughing about [reports we’re not close]. I was like, 'Who is telling people that?'
"On the flip side, I’ve heard we’re getting back together. I’ll deliver the truth with the doc. I’m always open [to that].
"Our divorce wasn’t messy. We were able to move on and be the best parents we can.
"I always say Mariah Carey was my greatest friend and my greatest teacher. What I learned most from her is how to hold on to what’s true and create your own spaces, without letting outside energy infiltrate.
"I’ve never seen somebody operate on their own frequency, and it’s always so positive. And you know all that she’s been through in her life. I think that’s what keeps her going — her faith and her ability to block out negative energy. You feel like you know her, but she keeps all the things that are meaningful to her to herself."
However, Nick isn't interested in getting married again.
He said: "I don’t like the government in my love life. I think the institution of marriage should be respected, but I can’t see myself going through the legal paperwork again."
The 45-year-old star is known for his colourful personal life because, as well as Moroccan and Monroe, he is also a father to Golden, nine, Powerful, five, and Rise, four, with Brittany Bell; five-year-old twins Zion and Zillion, and Beautiful, three, with Abby De La Rosa; Legendary, four, with Bre Tiesi; Onyx, four, with LaNisha Cole; and Halo, three, with Alyssa Scott, the mom of his late son Zen, who died of cancer aged just five months in 2021.
While Nick doesn't have a "favourite" among the moms of his children, he admitted he has a particularly special bond with Bre.
Asked if he and Bre are together, he said: "I’m gonna take this opportunity to clear this up because I get in trouble a lot.
"The person who understands me the most would be Bre. We call each other twin flames because she accepts all of my s***, and I accept [her].
"There’s a sense of understanding I don’t have with anybody else. She’s super protective of me. You can’t buy that type of loyalty.
"She believes I should have a hierarchy system.
"As much as I say I don’t have a favourite, she definitely holds a special place in my heart."

item.title: [The Hamilton County Reporter] The sixth Love Language
item.dc:creator: Amy Shankland
item.description: Many readers may be familiar with Gary Chapman’s excellent 1992 book, The Five Love Languages: The Secret to Love That Lasts. While I had heard of the book, I didn’t read it until a few years ago. If you don’t know Chapman’s five love languages, they include: - Words of Affirmation - Physical Touch - Receiving Gifts - Quality Time - Acts of Service My best friend Stacey recommended the book when John and I encountered a rocky patch – a common occurrence in most marriages. item.content:encoded:
Many readers may be familiar with Gary Chapman’s excellent 1992 book, The Five Love Languages: The Secret to Love That Lasts. While I had heard of the book, I didn’t read it until a few years ago.
If you don’t know Chapman’s five love languages, they include:
- Words of Affirmation
- Physical Touch
- Receiving Gifts
- Quality Time
- Acts of Service
My best friend Stacey recommended the book when John and I encountered a rocky patch – a common occurrence in most marriages. I’m grateful to her because it helped us back then and continues to help us now.
John and I enjoyed talked about and discovering our top love languages. Conveniently for us, Words of Affirmation are both number one. Acts of Service is number two for me, while Quality Time is John’s.
Recently, however, John and I have figured out there’s a sixth love language – well, at least for us. We would call it Cooking Meals. Now, you may argue cooking meals fits in the category of Acts of Service or even Receiving Gifts. But we feel it’s a whole other level.
We all must eat. But sometimes in this busy world, the thought of having to cook anything is overwhelming. Sure, we can turn to fast food, takeout, frozen dinners, etc. But of course, this comes at a cost, both financially and sometimes nutritionally.
I remember how I felt when people brought over homemade meals right after I gave birth to each of my two sons. This time of life was incredibly overwhelming, and to cross “dinner” off the list for a day was huge.
John and I genuinely enjoy planning and cooking meals for the people we love. We’re blessed to cook dinner every Sunday for our son Jonathon and his significant other, Olivia. It’s fun to brainstorm new ideas and see the look of joy on their faces when we present the meal.
Our kitchen is rather small, so working together takes some coordination. But cooking is a weekend tradition John and I love. And bonus – I’m a “clean as you go” cook. So, the kitchen ends up looking less like a war zone when we finally put dinner on the table.
This love language is what motivated me to join Lasagna Love years ago. While I no longer am in the program (since I’m always discovering people in my own city who need meals) I highly recommend the organization if Cooking Meals is one of your love languages. Check ‘em out at lasagnalove.org.
One new thing I enjoy doing is praying for the people who will eat the meal I create. I feel it adds an extra layer of love.
Hats off to Mr. Chapman for such a life-changing concept and book. May we all learn our own Love Languages and spread their joy to those around us.
Amy Shankland is an empty-nester, writer, and fundraising professional living in Noblesville with her husband John and two dogs. You can reach her via email at amys@greenavenue.info.

I need to stop helping her financially because it’s affecting m
item.content:encoded:
Dear Abby: I am a widow who lost my husband 15 years ago. When my husband died, we had a daughter and one grandson. My daughter, a single mom, later had another son.
I have my own business and have worked hard these many years to help support my daughter, who is financially irresponsible. She has been evicted four times in the past 10 years, had two cars repossessed and can’t seem to keep a job for even a year. I am at my wits’ end. I need to stop helping her financially because it’s affecting my financial and mental health.
She doesn’t have a job and can’t get her own place, so I feel I have no choice but to let her move in with me. I want to put a limit on how long she can stay. What should I do? — Subjugated in Texas
Dear Subjugated: Do not allow your daughter to move in with you. If she does, you will never get rid of her. Give her a certain amount of money for shelter and make it plain that she must use it to find a place to live (if only temporarily). Because it’s the last handout she’ll receive, she must get a job to support herself and her children. Then let her live the life she has chosen for herself. If you don’t, you will be your dysfunctional daughter’s prisoner until the day you die.
Dear Abby: Throughout my professional career, I was a quality assurance engineer with the task of analysis and corrective actions. If something broke or an error was made (for example, a worker’s hand getting caught in a machine), I’d try to identify a fix so it wouldn’t happen again. I am now retired and still tend to approach things with the same attitude.
I often get frustrated when someone makes an error and there’s no corrective action, admission that a mistake was made or even a small apology. I recently discovered an error on my financial accounts and asked the bank how this was overlooked even after I had pointed out the error prior to the account being processed. Abby, I was completely ignored and never received any feedback. What’s the best way to ask someone for an explanation concerning what actions were taken to ensure the error does not happen again? — Keen on Quality
Dear Keen on Quality: In your line of work, safety was the top priority. You developed a zero-tolerance attitude toward errors because it was literally a matter of life and limb. Outside that environment, however, you may find it helpful to remember that the stakes are not nearly so high.
No permanent harm came of the bank error. You are right that it would be best if the bank reviewed its procedures to avoid future errors, but that’s their job, not yours. Having corrected the error in a timely fashion, the bank owes you no further explanation. Trust that, in the future, they will do their best to improve without your help (but always check your statements).
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

The Olympic alpine skier took to Instagram to share photos with her 30-year-old beau, who is a French alpine skier, and included several snaps of the pair vacationing together in a tropical location. item.content:encoded:
Lindsey Vonn debuted her new romance with fellow skier Matthieu Bailet on Wednesday in a social media post that sent her fans into a frenzy.
The Olympic alpine skier took to Instagram to share photos with her 30-year-old beau, who is a French alpine skier, and included several snaps of the pair vacationing together in a tropical location.
In one photo, the happy couple stood in the crystal-clear waters of a pool overlooking the sea and shared a sweet kiss, with Lindsey in a white bikini and Matthieu in light-colored swim shorts.
Another picture showcased the pair standing on a rock in the ocean as Matthieu held Lindsey from behind. The 41-year-old ended the carousel of photos with a snap of the pair cozying up together as they laid out over the water.
"About that time for a summer recap… pt 1," she wrote in the caption, as her friends and fans rushed to the comment section to exclaim over the new romance.
"Can't wait to see the summer recap part 2," Matthieu joked, alongside a kissing emoji, while Olympian Ilona Maher added: "The award for the hottest couple goes to…"
Tennis star Sloane Stephens chimed in: "HARD LAUNCH!!!!!!!" while another fan said: "Beautiful couple – wish you both all the best!"
Lindsey and Matthieu were first linked in May when they were seen spending time together in NYC. He competed in the Winter Olympic Games in China in 2022, and made his World Cup debut in 2016 in Switzerland.
Learn more about Lindsey below...
Moving on from Diego
Lindsey most recently dated businessman Diego Osorio from 2021 to 2025, and opened up about moving on after their heartbreaking split.
"Valentine's Day will look a little different for me this year...but I have my two dogs, so they'll be my Valentine's dates," she told People.
"I think with everything that's going on in my life, I sometimes have to keep reminding myself that it's a tough road, but I'm doing what I love to do, and I'm very lucky to be able to do it. But it doesn't mean that it's easy, and doesn't mean that it's not lonely at times."
Lindsey's dating history
Before Diego, the blonde beauty dated NHL star P.K. Subban from 2017 to 2020, former Los Angeles Rams coach Kenan Smith from 2016 to 2017, and Tiger Woods from 2013 to 2015.
The pro golfer announced their romance on Facebook in March 2013, writing: "Something nice that's happened off the course was meeting Lindsey Vonn. Lindsey and I have been friends for some time, but over the last few months we have become very close and are now dating."
"We thank you for your support and for respecting our privacy. We want to continue our relationship, privately as an ordinary couple and continue to compete as athletes."
Lindsey was married to pro skier Thomas Vonn from 2007 to 2011, and shared that their relationship taught her "a lot".
"I'm thankful for my years with Thomas," she told The New York Times. "So this is a difficult time. But I'm not worried that I can't be successful without him. I'm a strong and capable woman."
