item.content:encoded:
If you’re looking for a serious relationship, dating apps can start to feel like a particularly exhausting game of “What the hell are you actually looking for?” Sure, their profile says “long-term relationship,” but does that mean marriage? A committed partner? Someone to split a Costco membership with? Or someone who will text you “wyd” every Thursday night for the next six months?
The good news is that people absolutely do use dating apps to find real, long-term relationships. And while certain apps are designed to make finding a serious partner easier, there’s no single app that magically contains all the people ready to commit. “Any dating app or website can be good for long-term relationships if you are honest and intentional about what you want from the beginning,” says Rachel Needle, PsyD, a licensed psychologist and co-director of Modern Sex Therapy Institutes.
Still, choosing an app that attracts people looking for the same kind of relationship you are can save you a whole lot of time. Just as important is making your own intentions clear. Clinical sexologist Tatyannah King, MSW, recommends explicitly stating that you’re looking for something long-term in your profile, even if doing so means getting fewer matches. She also suggests including specific details that actually tell people something about your life and personality. Basically, you’re trying to find someone compatible, not collect every available human within a 15-mile radius.
Ready to get back out there? Below, we’re breaking down the best dating apps for serious relationships, who they’re best for, what they cost, and what you should know before downloading.
1. Bumble
Best For:
Women who want more control over how conversations start.
Why We Picked It:
“Bumble is an ideal app for people who are looking for long-term partnerships, especially for women who date men,” King says. “As someone who dates with intention and prefers long-term relationships over short flings, I’ve personally also found it helpful to pay for the premium version. I noticed that men who are paying for the premium version of Bumble’s dating app seem to be more intentional about dating.”
She also loves Bumble’s Opening Moves feature, which lets women set prompts that their matches can respond to, giving them another way to get a conversation going beyond sending the first message themselves. Matches expire if no one sends a message within 24 hours, which can help keep things moving instead of letting a promising match sit untouched for three weeks.
Who It’s For:
Bumble is open to daters of all genders and orientations. In heterosexual matches, women traditionally initiate the conversation, but Opening Moves gives them the option to set a prompt that a match can respond to instead. In same-gender and nonbinary connections, either person can start the conversation.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
Pros:
- Opening Moves gives women more flexibility over how conversations get started
- Snooze Mode lets you temporarily hide your profile when you need a dating-app break
- Plenty of prompts and profile features to help show off your personality
- SuperSwipes let you signal extra interest in a potential match
- Incognito Mode lets Premium and Premium+ members only be seen by people they’ve already liked
- Paid subscriptions offer perks like unlimited likes and advanced filters
- Travel Mode lets Premium and Premium+ members change their location before or during a trip
Cons:
- The 24-hour window to start a conversation can feel limiting if you don’t check the app regularly
- Some of the most useful features, including Incognito and Travel Mode, require a paid subscription
- Bumble’s conversation rules can take a minute to get used to if you’re coming from apps where anyone can immediately message a match
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Bumble Boost starts at around $14.99 per week
- Bumble Premium starts at around $27.99 per week
- Bumble Premium+ starts at around $39.99 per week
2. Hinge
Best For:
Daters who want to know more than someone’s height and favorite vacation spot before matching.
Why We Picked It:
The self-proclaimed “dating app designed to be deleted,” Hinge is an obvious contender if your ultimate goal is to get off dating apps altogether. “If you're searching for a dating platform that prioritizes depth over quick swipes, Hinge might be just what you're looking for,” says Mariah Freya, sex education expert and founder of Beducated. “It combines the best of Tinder's ease of use with Match's focus on genuine connections.”
Profiles include photos and videos, answers to prompts, and details like dating intentions and relationship type, giving you plenty to work with when deciding whether you might actually like someone. You can also like or comment on a specific part of someone’s profile rather than simply swiping on the whole person, and Hinge’s newer Convo Starters feature offers personalized suggestions based on a match’s profile when your brain simply cannot come up with another opening line.
Who It’s For:
Hinge is open to daters of all genders and orientations, but it’s particularly useful if you want more information about potential matches upfront and are looking for something beyond a hookup.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
Pros:
- Detailed profiles include photos, videos, voice, prompts, dating intentions, and relationship preferences
- You can like or comment on specific parts of someone’s profile, giving you a built-in conversation starter
- Convo Starters can help when you have absolutely no idea what to say
- Selfie Verification can help confirm that matches look like the person in their profile
- Hinge’s We Met feature asks about your dates after you exchange phone numbers with a match and uses that feedback to improve future recommendations
- Hinge+ offers unlimited likes and lets you see everyone who has liked you
- HingeX adds features like enhanced recommendations and Priority Likes
Cons:
- Free users have a limited number of likes
- Some of the features that make Hinge significantly easier to use are behind paid subscriptions
- Detailed profiles are great if you want depth, less great if filling out dating-app prompts is your personal hell
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Hinge+ starts at around $29.99 per month
- HingeX starts at around $49.99 per month
3. Tinder
Best For:
Having a ton of options.
Why We Picked It:
Tinder is basically the reason swiping became synonymous with dating apps in the first place, and its sheer size is still one of its biggest selling points. The app is available in more than 190 countries and has racked up more than 55 billion matches, so if your biggest dating problem is simply finding enough people to date, Tinder certainly gives you options. And while it has a reputation as a hookup app, you can specify what you’re looking for with Relationship Goals, including a long-term partner.
Who It’s For:
Tinder is open to daters of all genders and orientations and is a particularly good option if you want a large dating pool. Because people use Tinder for everything from casual hookups to serious relationships, though, pay attention to Relationship Goals and be upfront about what you’re looking for if long-term love is the goal.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop via Tinder for Web
Pros:
- Huge dating pool with users around the world
- Easy to set up and start swiping
- Relationship Goals help you communicate what you’re looking for
- Photo Verification lets users verify that they look like their profile photos
- Rewind lets subscribers undo their last Like or Nope
- Passport Mode lets you change your location and match with people elsewhere
- Tinder Platinum includes Priority Likes, which helps your Likes and Super Likes get seen faster
Cons:
- A huge dating pool also means more profiles to wade through
- People use Tinder for all kinds of connections, so not everyone you encounter will be looking for a serious relationship
- Free users don’t get unlimited Likes
- Features like Rewind and Passport require a subscription or separate purchase
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Tinder Plus starts at around $9.99 per month
- Tinder Gold starts at around $13.99 per month
4. Hily
Best For:
Gen Z daters looking for a more intentional, inclusive dating experience.
Why We Picked It:
With a large Gen Z user base, Hily is clearly geared toward younger daters. The app has more than 43 million downloads and puts a big emphasis on authenticity, compatibility, and helping users find people who are actually looking for the same things they are.
One feature that especially stands out is Consent Guard, which is designed to help prevent unsolicited explicit messages and images. If the technology detects potentially sexual content, it prompts the sender to ask for consent before sending it, giving the recipient the option to accept or decline. Because nothing kills the possibility of a meaningful connection quite like an unsolicited nude from someone you exchanged three messages with.
Who It’s For:
Hily is especially suited to Gen Z daters who want to meet people based on more than a few carefully curated photos. It may also appeal to anyone who appreciates extra control over the kinds of sexual messages or images they receive while dating online.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
Pros:
- Particularly geared toward Gen Z and younger daters
- Consent Guard helps prevent unsolicited explicit messages and photos from reaching you without your consent
- Discover offers another way to find potential matches based on your interests and dating intentions
- Profile verification and other safety features help screen potential matches
- Compatibility features offer another way to evaluate potential matches beyond their photos
- You can add music to your profile, because music compatibility is very much a thing
Cons:
- Some features require a paid subscription
- May appeal less to older daters looking for a more traditional dating-app experience
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Hily Premium starts at around $14.99 per week
- Hily Premium+ starts at around $24.99 per week
- Additional in-app purchases, including profile boosts, are available
5. eharmony
Best For:
Daters who are serious about finding a long-term partner.
Why We Picked It:
eharmony has been around since 2000, which is approximately 400 years in dating-app time, but its focus on long-term compatibility is also what keeps it relevant for people who are serious about finding a relationship. Instead of immediately throwing you into an endless stack of profiles, the app has you complete a detailed Compatibility Quiz and uses your answers to generate matches and compatibility information.
“If you're ready to say ‘I do,’ then eharmony is there to guide you along the way,” Freya says. “Renowned for its emphasis on long-term commitment, it's like the Charlotte York of dating apps—traditional and mostly geared towards heterosexual relationships.” While you certainly don’t need to be ready for marriage tomorrow to use it, the more involved setup process and detailed profiles may appeal to daters who are willing to put a little more time into finding a compatible partner.
Who It’s For:
People looking for a serious, long-term relationship who don’t mind spending more time setting up their profile and answering compatibility questions upfront. It may also appeal to daters who prefer a more structured matching process over simply swiping through profiles.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop
Pros:
- Detailed profiles and an in-depth Compatibility Quiz
- Compatibility information can help you evaluate potential matches
- Matching process is designed around long-term compatibility
- Particularly geared toward relationship-minded daters
- Free Basic membership lets you create a profile and browse matches
Cons:
- More time-consuming to set up than swipe-first apps
- Unlimited messaging and several other features require Premium
- Premium subscriptions require a longer commitment than many competing apps
- May feel a little traditional compared with newer dating apps
Price:
- Free Basic membership available
- Premium Light, typically a six-month commitment, runs roughly $59 to $69 per month
- Premium Plus, typically a 12-month commitment, runs roughly $38 to $50 per month
- Premium Extra, typically a 24-month commitment, runs roughly $29 to $33 per month
6. Match
Best For:
Serious daters who want a large, established dating pool.
Why We Picked It:
Match has been around since 1995, making it one of the OG online dating platforms—and there’s something to be said for an app that has survived approximately every era of internet dating. Unlike platforms that lean heavily into casual swiping, Match has long positioned itself toward people looking for relationships.
“Match is my top choice for its ability to cater to individuals in their 30s and 40s seeking meaningful connections,” Freya says. “Its large user base offers a wide range of like-minded adults looking for genuine relationships.” Profiles also give you plenty of space to spell out who you are and what you’re looking for, which can be especially useful when the goal is finding someone you might actually want to date long-term.
Who It’s For:
Relationship-minded daters who want a more traditional online dating experience and plenty of information about potential matches before deciding whether to connect.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop
Pros:
- Large, established dating pool
- Detailed profiles let you learn more about potential matches upfront
- Geared toward people looking for relationships
- Search and filtering options can help narrow down potential matches
Cons:
- Many features require a paid subscription
- Can feel more traditional than newer dating apps
- Paid memberships can get pricey
- Longer subscriptions are generally billed upfront rather than month-to-month
Price:
- Free to join and use with limited features
- Standard plans run roughly $34.45 per month for three months, $24.48 per month for six months, or $21.84 per month for 12 months
- Premium plans run roughly $40.41 per month for three months, $26.51 per month for six months, or $23.11 per month for 12 months
- Multi-month plans are generally charged in full at the beginning of the subscription
7. OkCupid
Best For:
Daters who want to get specific about compatibility.
Why We Picked It:
OkCupid has been around since 2004, but it’s managed to evolve beyond its early-internet-dating roots. One of its biggest draws is the sheer number of questions you can answer about everything from relationships and lifestyle to politics, sex, and approximately whatever else you might want to know about someone before agreeing to spend two hours across a table from them.
Your answers help determine your compatibility with potential matches, and you can also specify what kind of relationship you’re looking for. That makes OkCupid especially useful if you have particular values, preferences, or dealbreakers you’d rather get out of the way sooner rather than later.
Who It’s For:
Daters who want a more inclusive app and like having plenty of information about potential matches upfront. It’s also a good option if you’d rather use compatibility questions to narrow down your dating pool than rely primarily on photos and a few prompts.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop
Pros:
- Lots of compatibility questions to help you find people with similar values and preferences
- Inclusive gender and sexual-orientation options
- You can specify the type of relationship you’re looking for
- Free version offers plenty of functionality
- Available on desktop as well as mobile
Cons:
- Answering enough questions to get the most out of the compatibility features takes some time
- Some features and filters require a paid subscription
- The amount of information can feel like a lot if you prefer a simpler swipe-and-go experience
Price:
- Free to download and use
- OkCupid Premium starts at around $19.99 per month
- Additional paid features and Boosts are available
8. Flure
Best For:
Sex-positive daters looking for less traditional dating-app rules.
Why We Picked It:
A serious relationship doesn’t necessarily have to follow the traditional dating-app playbook, which is where Flure comes in. The app takes a more open-ended approach to dating, encouraging users to meet people and see where the connection goes rather than requiring them to define exactly what they’re looking for upfront. It also puts a particular emphasis on sex positivity, inclusivity, and creating a space where users can be open about what they want.
Flure also puts an emphasis on safety and communication. Its in-app features include Safe Mode, which helps protect users from unsolicited explicit content, and Flure Sparks, a game designed to help matches get to know each other and talk about everything from everyday interests to sex and relationships.
Who It’s For:
Sex-positive and open-minded daters who prefer a less rigid approach to defining what they’re looking for and want an app that leaves room for different kinds of connections.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS
Pros:
- Open-ended approach lets connections develop without requiring a relationship label upfront
- Flure Sparks offers built-in prompts to help matches get to know each other
- Safe Mode adds another layer of protection against unsolicited explicit content
- Welcoming to people looking for connections outside the traditional dating-app mold
Cons:
- Smaller dating pool than more established apps
- Its intentionally label-free approach may not appeal to daters who want to filter specifically for a long-term relationship from the start
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Premium costs around $29.99 per month
- Three-month subscriptions cost around $44.99
- Annual subscriptions cost around $107.99
9. BLK
Best For:
Black singles looking for meaningful connections.
Why We Picked It:
BLK is a dating and lifestyle app created specifically with the Black community in mind, giving Black singles a space to meet people without having to rely solely on the filters and preferences offered by more general dating apps. And if you’re looking for a serious relationship, being able to start with a dating pool centered around a shared cultural experience can make finding compatible matches a little easier.
The app also goes beyond one-on-one matching with BLK Community, which includes chat rooms organized around different interests and topics, giving users another way to connect beyond simply swiping through profiles.
Who It’s For:
Black singles looking to date, build relationships, and connect with other members of the Black community.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
Pros:
- Created specifically with Black singles in mind
- BLK Community offers chat rooms based on shared interests
- Super Likes let you signal extra interest in someone
- Rewind lets paid members go back if they accidentally pass on someone
- Paid tiers offer perks like unlimited likes, Boosts, and the ability to see who likes you
Cons:
- Smaller dating pool than major mainstream apps
- Some of the most useful features require a paid membership
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Premium starts at around $9.99 per week
- Elite starts at around $21.99 per week
- Platinum starts at around $29.99 per week or $49.99 per month
10. Plenty of Fish
Best For:
Daters who actually want to talk before meeting up.
Why We Picked It:
Plenty of Fish has been around since 2003, so it’s another dating app that predates swiping as we know it. But if you’re looking for something serious, its emphasis on conversation can be a plus. Rather than making every interaction feel like a split-second decision based on a few photos, POF gives users plenty of ways to actually talk and get to know potential matches.
The app also has an “Are You Sure?” feature designed to detect potentially inappropriate language and give you a chance to reconsider a message before sending it. Because sometimes the difference between a promising match and an immediate unmatch is simply taking two seconds to reread what you typed.
Who It’s For:
Daters who prefer getting to know someone through conversation and want an app that feels a little less focused on endlessly swiping through profiles.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop
Pros:
- Conversation-focused features make it easier to get to know matches
- “Are You Sure?” encourages users to reconsider potentially inappropriate messages before sending
- Search features let you get more specific about what you’re looking for
- Large, established dating platform
- Free version lets you access many of the app’s core features
Cons:
- Interface may feel a little dated compared with newer dating apps
- Some features require a paid membership
Price:
- Free to download and use
- POF Premium starts at around $29.99 per month
- One-week subscriptions are available for around $19.99
- Additional Tokens and other in-app purchases are available
11. Happn
Best For:
Meeting someone you might actually cross paths with IRL.
Why We Picked It:
If you’d ideally like to date someone who lives in your general vicinity, Happn puts a digital spin on the old-school meet-cute. The location-based app helps you discover people you’ve crossed paths with IRL, whether that’s someone who frequents the same coffee shop, lives in your neighborhood, or apparently has the exact same Target schedule you do.
For daters looking for something serious, there’s an obvious practical upside: Your matches are already spending time in the same places you are. And while Happn can’t guarantee you’ll end up in a rom-com-worthy meet-cute, it can make meeting someone nearby a little easier than waiting to dramatically bump into a hot stranger on the sidewalk.
Who It’s For:
Daters who want to meet people nearby and like the idea of connecting with someone they may already cross paths with in their everyday life.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop via the Happn web app
Pros:
- Location-based matching helps you find people you’ve crossed paths with
- Particularly useful if dating someone nearby is important to you
- You can use Happn on desktop via its web app
- Boost can increase your profile’s visibility
- Offers a more IRL-inspired approach to discovering potential matches
Cons:
- Smaller dating pool than some of the biggest dating apps
- Less useful in areas where there aren’t many active users
- Location-based matching means you may encounter some of the same profiles repeatedly
- Not ideal if you’re primarily interested in meeting people outside your area
Price:
- Free to download and use
- Happn Premium subscriptions are available
- Boosts and other in-app purchases are also available
12. HER
Best For:
Queer women, lesbians, and nonbinary daters.
Why We Picked It:
HER bills itself as “the sapphic dating app,” and unlike mainstream dating apps that simply offer LGBTQ+ identity and preference settings, the platform was built specifically around queer dating and community. That can make a pretty major difference when you’re looking for a serious relationship and would rather not spend half your time figuring out whether someone is actually available to date you.
“HER isn't your average dating app—it's a vibrant community and dating platform designed specifically for queer women and non-binary individuals,” Freya says. “If you've ever felt out of place or uncomfortable on mainstream apps, HER offers a safe haven. It's a welcoming space where you can truly be yourself and connect with like-minded queer folks who understand your experiences.”
Who It’s For:
Lesbian, bisexual, queer, and other sapphic women, as well as nonbinary and trans daters who identify with the community HER serves.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
Pros:
- Built specifically for sapphic and queer dating
- Offers community features in addition to one-on-one matching
- Helps users discover queer events and gatherings
- Gives users plenty of gender identity and sexuality options
- Free version includes core matching, messaging, events, and community features
Cons:
- Not designed for straight daters or cisgender men
- Some filters and additional features require a paid subscription
- Unlimited swiping requires a paid membership
Price:
- Free to download and use
- HER Premium starts at around $14.99 per month
13. EliteSingles
Best For:
Career-minded daters looking for something serious.
Why We Picked It:
If career, education, and ambition are high on your list of things you’d like to have in common with a partner, EliteSingles is built around helping you find people with similar priorities. The app is geared specifically toward relationship-minded singles and uses a personality questionnaire and your dating preferences to recommend compatible matches.
“If you're a go-getter in both your career and personal life and find the usual dating apps a bit uninspiring, EliteSingles might be just what you need,” Freya says. “It's like the exclusive club of dating apps—perfect for ambitious, successful individuals seeking genuine connections. While the membership fee may be higher, it serves as a barrier, ensuring you meet people who are as serious about finding a partner as you are.”
Who It’s For:
Daters who are looking for a long-term relationship and particularly interested in meeting other career- and education-minded singles.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS and Android
- Available on desktop
Pros:
- Geared specifically toward people looking for serious relationships
- Personality questionnaire helps inform your match recommendations
- Particularly focused on career- and education-minded singles
- Detailed profiles give you more information about potential matches upfront
Cons:
- Free membership is fairly limited
- Smaller dating pool than major mainstream apps
- Premium membership can be expensive
- Not ideal if you prefer browsing a huge pool of matches on your own
Price:
- Free Basic membership available with limited features
- Premium costs around $64.99 for one month
- Three-month Premium membership costs around $34.99 per month
- Six-month Premium membership costs around $28.33 per month
- Multi-month subscriptions are charged upfront
14. Beyond
Best For:
Polyamorous and ethically non-monogamous daters.
Why We Picked It:
Looking for a serious relationship doesn’t necessarily mean looking for a monogamous one. Beyond is an inclusive, members-only dating app that lets users specify and filter by relationship style as well as sexual orientation, making it particularly useful for polyamorous and ethically non-monogamous daters who want to be upfront about what they’re looking for.
“I’d suggest Beyond because it has more of a social element that most apps are missing,” King says. “Beyond’s core mission is to ‘curate a community for honest and intentional dating.’ Because of its mission, the founders host consistent in-person meetups for users in various cities in the U.S., which creates a more organic dating experience that naturally leads to creating a solid connection.”
Who It’s For:
Sex-positive and community-minded daters, particularly those who are polyamorous, ethically non-monogamous, or looking for other nontraditional relationship structures.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS
Pros:
- Lets you filter by dating preference, including monogamous, monogamish, open, polyamorous, exploring, and looking for friends
- Lets you filter by sexuality, gender, and relationship status
- Hosts IRL events and meetups in select cities
- Members go through an application process before joining
- Community-focused approach offers ways to connect beyond traditional swiping
Cons:
- Currently only available on iOS
- IRL events aren’t available everywhere
- Membership approval can take some time
- Smaller dating pool than mainstream apps
- May not be the best fit if you’re specifically looking for a traditional monogamous relationship
Price:
- Free to download
- Weekly memberships start at around $14.99
- Monthly memberships start at around $19.99
- Three-month memberships cost around $74.99
- Additional purchases, including Direct Requests and Skip the Wait, are available
15. The League
Best For:
Career-focused daters looking for an equally ambitious partner.
Why We Picked It:
If your career is a major part of your life and you’d like to date someone who gets that, The League is built specifically around connecting ambitious, career-minded singles. Unlike apps where you can download and immediately start swiping, The League has an application process and may place prospective members on a waitlist before they’re admitted.
That extra barrier to entry won’t be for everyone, but if you’re looking for a serious relationship with someone who has similar professional priorities, the more curated dating pool may be part of the appeal.
Who It’s For:
Career-focused singles who want to meet other ambitious daters and don’t mind a more selective application process.
Platform Info:
- Available on iOS
Pros:
- Geared toward ambitious, career-focused daters
- Application process creates a more curated dating pool
- Offers a curated daily batch of potential matches rather than an endless stream of profiles
- Particularly useful if career compatibility matters to you in a long-term partner
Cons:
- Application and waitlist mean you may not be able to start matching immediately
- Smaller dating pool than mainstream apps
- Memberships can be significantly more expensive than other dating apps
- The selective, career-focused approach may not appeal to everyone
Price:
- Free membership available
- Paid memberships start at around $59.99 per week or $99.99 per month
- Additional purchases, including extra prospects, League Tickets, and profile Boosts, are available

item.title: [usmagazine.com] Tom Parker’s Widow Kelsey Parker and Boyfriend Will Lindsay’s Relationship Timeline
item.dc:creator: Kaitlin Simpson; Elise Nelson
item.description: Tom Parker’s widow Kelsey Parker found a second chance at love with boyfriend Will Lindsay while coping with grief. item.content:encoded:
Tom Parker’s widow Kelsey Parker found a second chance at love with boyfriend Will Lindsay while coping with grief.
Kelsey and Tom were married from 2018 until his death in March 2022 at age 33. The Wanted member died following his battle with brain cancer. Kelsey and Tom welcomed two children, Aurelia and Bodhi, in July 2019 and October 2020, respectively.
Years after Tom’s passing, Kelsey shared that she was dating again and revealed her new romance with Lindsay in September 2024. Four months later, Kelsey announced that she was pregnant with her and Lindsay’s first child.
“Tom and I always said we wanted four — but life had other plans,” she told The Mirror in January 2025. “So yes, this is amazing but also bittersweet. The joys of finding out I’m pregnant and moving forward with my life, while thinking, ‘My life could have been so different. I’ve felt every emotion under the sun.”
In June 2025, Kelsey announced the loss of their baby, sharing that he was “born sleeping.”
“Phoenix Parker-Lindsay, you will forever be loved,” she wrote via Instagram at the time.
Keep scrolling for a complete timeline of Kelsey and Lindsay’s relationship:
September 2024
Two years after Tom’s death, Kelsey made her Lindsay’s romance Instagram Official. The post included a photo of the couple hugging while Lindsay’s head turned away from the camera and was captioned with a single red heart emoji. After making their relationship official, Kelsey took to social media to thank fans for their kind words.
“I was really hesitant to share this part of my life, especially since many of you know me from my life with Tom and the horrific grief I’ve been dealing with after losing him,” she penned. “Opening up about my journey over the past couple of years has been incredibly healing, allowing me to connect with others who’ve gone through similar experiences and build a beautiful, supportive community.”
October 2024
During an October 2024 episode of Kelsey’s “Mum’s the Word” podcast with Georgia Jones, Kelsey shared that she and Lindsay “met authentically” and they had already introduced each other to their families.
“He just makes me really happy. And I think for me, I’ve been trying to find happiness for a little while now. I’m always going to have that guilt, I guess that’s part of the grief process.” she explained. “Having the guilt that I’m here and I’ve met someone but it will never take away the love I had for Tom. And with Will he would never try and take that away from me either.”
November 2024
While appearing on the British talk show Lorraine, Kelsey gave some more details about how she and Lindsay first connected.
“We met out with friends, he was out with a group of boys and I was out with a group of girls and we just had a connection,” she gushed. “I just wanted to meet someone authentic. I couldn’t have done [a] dating app, I was so scared and it was the judgment from people about moving on and meeting someone, but everyone’s so supportive.”
January 2025
Kelsey and Lindsay announced that they were expecting their first child together.
“I’m over the moon. This is something I’ve wanted for a long time,” Lindsay told The Mirror. “I couldn’t be happier and I know Kelsey is going to be an amazing mum, as she already is.”
April 2025
Lindsay and Kelsey took a family trip to Gran Canaria, Spain.
“Nothing beats a family holiday to Gran Canaria!!” Kelsey wrote via Instagram alongside a photo of the family of the group out to dinner. “These trips will always have a special place in our hearts, we always have the best time ☀️ Soaking up these moments before our family grows… 🤰🏼.”
June 2025
Kelsey announced that she and Lindsay lost their baby, whom they named Phoenix. The post included a poem written in honor of the late newborn, who was born stillborn.
“For Phoenix, Born Sleeping, Forever Loved,” the poem began. “The world grew quiet as you arrived / So loved, so longed for, yet not alive / Our precious boy, our angel light / Born with wings, took silent flight. We named you Phoenix, brave and bright / A soul of love, of warmth and light / Though we never heard you cry / You’ll live in hearts that won’t ask why. No breath you drew, no eyes to see / Still, you mean everything to me / You’ll journey with us, softly near / In every sigh, in every tear.”
May 2026
Kelsey announced her pregnancy with her and Lindsay’s rainbow baby nearly one year after Phoenix’s death.
“A year ago next month, we lost our beautiful baby boy, Phoenix 🤍,” she wrote via Instagram. “And somehow, through all the heartbreak, it feels like Tom and Phoenix have sent us another little gift from heaven our little rainbow baby ✨.”
September 2026
Kelsey and Lindsay welcomed daughter River, calling her “our little bit of hope.”

item.title: [ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation] Dating app safety shouldn't be left to women, researchers say
item.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
item.dc:creator: Clare Armstrong
item.description: In short: Almost all women surveyed in a new Australian study reported encountering harmful behaviour on dating apps, with many taking their own precautions to stay safe. Researchers say platforms should do more to prevent systemic risks as the federal government considers a digital duty of care. What's next? Consultation on Labor's proposed digital duty of care closes on Tuesday, with advocates saying it has capacity to curb online abuse. Women are being forced to act as their own safety system
item.content:encoded:
In short:
Almost all women surveyed in a new Australian study reported encountering harmful behaviour on dating apps, with many taking their own precautions to stay safe.
Researchers say platforms should do more to prevent systemic risks as the federal government considers a digital duty of care.
What's next?
Consultation on Labor's proposed digital duty of care closes on Tuesday, with advocates saying it has capacity to curb online abuse.
Women are being forced to act as their own safety system on dating apps where experiences of sexual harassment, manipulation and controlling behaviours are widespread, a study has found.
Australian researchers found 99 per cent of heterosexual women surveyed had encountered at least one harmful behaviour on a dating app in the previous three months.
Unsolicited explicit messages, attempts to monitor activity, love bombing, negging and gaslighting are common experiences on dating apps, according to the study released on Tuesday by the Minderoo Foundation-funded Behaviour Insights Team (BIT).
Women reported routinely screening profiles for warning signs, withholding identifying information and carefully managing interactions to protect themselves from potential harm.
These accounts have fuelled calls to ensure a proposed digital duty of care was implemented to require online services to tackle systemic risks.
Researchers have argued the scale of the problem showed women could not be expected to manage the risks alone, with dating platforms better placed to prevent harm before it occurred.
Women coaching each other to stay safe
Brisbane resident Rebecca Wilson, 33, said her harmful dating app experiences have included receiving "completely unsolicited" and "aggressively sexual" messages, photos and videos.
Ms Wilson said she was also once stalked by a man she had met via an app.
"We went on one date. I said to him, 'Look I'm just not interested anymore', and he didn't get the message," she said.
"Weeks later he kept popping up at the same places as me … following me around.
"He touched me at a bar right in front of my friends when it was clearly unsolicited."
With only minimal information on the man, Ms Wilson said she could not easily report him to authorities.
One issue was that using the "block" feature on the app meant she lost the ability to collect identifying material to progress a complaint.
"There's no way of being able to know the identity of who you were talking to," Ms WIlson said.
Ms Wilson said she and her friends have "coached" each other through how to navigate online dating safely.
"The current mechanisms are really just not enough on these apps," she said.
Harmful behaviour 'normalised'
The most common harmful behaviours on dating apps were psychological and emotional, which were encountered by 95 per cent of the 1,008 women across Australia surveyed for the BIT study.
About 89 per cent experienced monitoring and surveillance activity and 88 per cent reported being sent unsolicited sexual images and videos, and being pressured and manipulated into sending sexual content.
Almost six in 10 women reported fear-based controlling behaviour, including threats of physical harm. Of those, only about 22 per cent reported those threats to the platforms.
Among women who made reports to platforms generally, about 19 per cent felt their complaint was "barely" or "not at all" taken seriously, while 64 per cent said they were taken at least "somewhat" seriously.
Lead researcher Karen Tindall said the findings showed there was a need for greater efforts by the platforms to tackle "genuinely preventable risk".
"Right now, a lot of these behaviours are so normalised that women blame themselves or they think they are overreacting," she said.
"This data and research should validate women's experience and should shift the conversation toward fixing the system itself."
Dr Tindall said there were features built for safety that could lead to harm, such as preventing screenshots to prevent against image-based abuse.
"But that also removes a woman's ability to document what happened," she said.
"I'm not saying those safety features should be removed, but it means that safety features need to be tested for how they will be worked around, and whether they will work as intended."
Duty would shift responsibility onto platforms
The findings have been released as the federal government consults on its proposed digital duty of care, which is intended to require services to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks rather than relying on users to report harm after the fact.
The draft duty for adults could apply to dating platforms on which users have faced serious abuse, stalking, sexual violence or image-based abuse.
It would mean services were required to identify and mitigate systemic risks that could enable such conduct.
While the initial debate has focused on social media, the proposed duty would apply more broadly across digital services, including dating and messaging apps, online games, search engines and AI services.
Minderoo Foundation gender equality executive director Jacqueline Joudo Larsen said a digital duty of care could prevent harm and protect Australians.
"It is the single biggest lever to curb the reach, scale and speed at which abuse is occurring by shifting responsibility from individuals to companies that are designing and operating online platforms," she said.
"This is a standard that we hold other sectors to and it should be no different for the online space."
Ms Larsen said technology had "transformed" how people met, connected and built relationships.
"Those benefits are very meaningful," she said.
"But safety cannot be the price women pay for participation.
"This is a design problem that's entirely preventable."
Ms Larsen said Australia could be a leader in tech safety and, if it was serious about ending sexual and domestic violence, that was an "opportunity we can't squander".
Labor's proposal under scrutiny
Submissions on Labor's proposal close on Tuesday and draft legislation will likely be introduced next month.
The Coalition has criticised the draft, primarily due to concerns over discretionary powers allowing the minister to add additional "harms" for children and "serious harms" for adults.
In a social media post shared by Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, the Coalition dubbed the idea the "Albo-rithm" and suggested the government would seek to censor online spaces.
But Communications Minister Anika Wells has repeatedly said the intent of the rule making power was about acting with "urgency" if new threats, such as apps that allowed users to "nudify" photos, arose online.
"We think this is a sensible measure to try and deal with these emerging harms that are coming online every single day," she said earlier this month.
The discretion in the bill for adding additional harms would be disallowable by the Senate at any time, but Labor might have to make some changes to their plan in order to secure the Greens' support for the draft bill.
In another submission to the draft legislation, the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman has described the reforms as a "rare opportunity" to build trust and accountability into the digital economy from the outset.
Ombudsman Cynthia Gebert said trust would not be built by hoping companies did the right thing and urged the government to consider an independent external dispute mechanism for when system failures occurred.
"Everyday Australians need someone to turn to for support holding big tech companies accountable when they get things wrong and we stand ready to help," she said.
The submission said an external complaints system would provide a "practical avenue" for Australians to resolve issues such as restoration of account access, ensuring choices about algorithms are implemented and reconsidering incorrect decisions.

item.title: [crash.net] Podcast: Has Pedro Acosta caused a shift in the MotoGP title fight?
item.dc:creator: Lewis Duncan
item.description: Pedro Acosta is finally a MotoGP race winner, after he took an emotional first victory at the Austrian Grand Prix on KTM’s home turf. The Spaniard had to wait 56 premier class starts before he could break his duck, something that seemed unfathomable when he made his debut at the start of the 2024 season. Acosta was quick from the off at the Red Bull Ring, but he had to win the grand prix the hard way on Sunday. A certain victory in the sprint was thrown away when he crashed with three laps to go
item.content:encoded:
Pedro Acosta is finally a MotoGP race winner, after he took an emotional first victory at the Austrian Grand Prix on KTM’s home turf.
The Spaniard had to wait 56 premier class starts before he could break his duck, something that seemed unfathomable when he made his debut at the start of the 2024 season.
Acosta was quick from the off at the Red Bull Ring, but he had to win the grand prix the hard way on Sunday.
A certain victory in the sprint was thrown away when he crashed with three laps to go, while he left his KTM team with more repair work to do on Sunday morning when he fell in warm-up.
But once he took the lead on lap nine of 28 in the main race, he never looked back, as he had the measure of Aprilia’s Jorge Martin.
It’s a win that closes a circle for the Acosta/KTM relationship, with the 22-year-old moving on to Ducati next season.
But could it get even better for both parties in the remaining races of 2026?
Though 72 points adrift in the standings, Marc Marquez firmly considers Acosta a title contender and has already branded him the favourite for the upcoming Japanese Grand Prix.
On the latest Crash MotoGP Podcast, Amy Reynolds is joined by Lewis Duncan and Peter McLaren to discuss the Austrian Grand Prix and whether or not Acosta can still fight for the 2026 title.
The team also discuss Acosta’s character and what to expect long-term when he goes up against Marc Marquez at Ducati in 2027.
Elsewhere, they discuss Jorge Martin’s strong weekend and his 12-point lead in the championship, asking if this is the Spaniard’s true return to form.
Ducati’s difficult weekend at the Red Bull Ring is analysed, as most of its riders were well off the pace, while Marc Marquez battled a brake issue in the grand prix.

item.title: [screenrant.com] 15 Best Movies About Marriage & Divorce
item.dc:creator: Karlis Wilde
item.description: Some of the best romance movies ever made have tackled some difficult territory, examining the complicated topics of marriage and divorce alike. While many of the most satisfying endings seen in film have closed happily, some of the strongest dramatic entries have taken a harder look at emotions, chronicling the difficult dissolutions of relationships and marriages. Movies about divorces are not always easy to watch. Many such stories delve into the complex emotional turmoil that the falling apa
item.content:encoded:
Some of the best romance movies ever made have tackled some difficult territory, examining the complicated topics of marriage and divorce alike. While many of the most satisfying endings seen in film have closed happily, some of the strongest dramatic entries have taken a harder look at emotions, chronicling the difficult dissolutions of relationships and marriages.
Movies about divorces are not always easy to watch. Many such stories delve into the complex emotional turmoil that the falling apart of a relationship can hold. Loaded with heartbreak and genuine pain, these stories provide deep points of connection that can help anyone going through such a struggle find ways to still feel human.
However, considering a marriage that ends in divorce to be a failure is such a limiting way of looking at the world.
Seeing the connections that blossom between two people, even if they do not last forever, is an important emotional factor in movies about humans and relationships. Not every love lasts forever, but this does not take away from the value that it has provided to a life.
Sometimes letting go of a relationship is worth celebrating, not just grieving. Many of these complex films examine the fallouts of those relationships in different and often surprising ways. Moving on is a part of life, and seeing how that works can fill these stories with sadness, joy, humor, and heartbreak all at once, making these films essential watches.
Divorce Italian Style
An unusual look at marriage and divorce, this fantastic 1961 comedy directed by Pietro Germi deeply questions a number of confusing social mores. In the film, Ferdinando, a poor Sicilian nobleman played by Marcello Mastroianni, falls in love with his sixteen-year-old cousin, Angela, and wishes to be with her.
However, Ferdinando is married, and divorce is illegal. However, considering the law's lax treatment of honor killings, he devises an absurd path to being with Angela: he will secretly find his wife a new lover, catch them in the act, and murder her. After serving a short prison sentence, he will be able to be with Angela.
This convoluted path highlights major issues with Italian law, and does so with great humor. A twisted and hilarious story, Divorce Italian Style is one of the more outsized and comedic looks at marriage and relationships on this list.
War Of The Roses
Danny DeVito has directed some fantastic films, and War of the Roses might be his best. This dark and funny 1989 comedy examines the dissolution of a marriage between Oliver and Barbara Rose, played by Michael Douglas and Kathleen Turner respectively. Rounding out the cast, DeVito plays their lawyer.
While the marriage between the Roses at first seems idyllic, cracks appear quickly and constantly throughout the film's runtime. The story turns into an unsettling war of a divorce that, while often hilarious, is also palpable in its cruelty, making the film a challenge for some to watch.
Still, based on a novel by Warren Adler, The War of the Roses is full of great substance, and is an entertaining, even if sometimes difficult, watch. The story was also recently remade in another strong film, 2025's The Roses.
A Separation
Global cinema has given excellent insight into how marriages and divorces function throughout the world, and A Separation is one of the strongest examples of this. Asghar Farhadi's 2011 Iranian drama was a huge achievement, and even won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
Built around family complications, the film sees Simin looking to leave Iran with their daughter in order to find a better life. Meanwhile, her husband wishes to stay, due to his father's medical needs. The film escalates, examining the complexities of family duties, immigration, and Iran's legal system.
A thoughtful film with a great deal to say, A Separation gives a fantastic look at relationships in Iran, and how even the most well-meaning characters can have their intentions corrupted by the machinations of separation.
Possession (1981)
The 1981 horror film Possession, which is itself being remade for 2027, is a fantastic entry in the genre. Sam Neill plays Mark, a spy who returns home only to learn that his wife, Anna, is sleeping with someone else and wishes to file for divorce.
The film leans into the texture of its Cold War setting, and highlights great feelings of alienation.
As a horror film, Possession goes to some interesting places. Director Andrzej Żuławski uses supernatural horrors in the film to express the psychological destruction of a relationship falling apart, as Mark discovers a terrifying creature with some shocking implications for the film's story.
Terrifying and raw all at once, the human story behind Possession is what makes it so strong. A horror with fantastic depth, it is an essential genre watch in the canon of films about divorce.
Kramer Vs. Kramer
Movies about heartbreak are necessarily difficult, but they can also show growth in unexpected ways. The 1979 legal drama Kramer vs. Kramer is a fantastic example of this, built around the separation and eventual divorce of Ted and Joanna Kramer, played by Dustin Hoffman and Meryl Streep, respectively.
The film took an unprecedented look at gender roles, uniquely examining a father's place in caring for his child. When Joanna suddenly decides to leave her marriage, it is up to Ted to stay behind and commit himself to his relationship with his son, giving the child a loving home throughout devastating emotional turmoil.
Giving eyes into a contentious battle for custody, the film shows the ruthlessness that a divorce can bring out between two people who love one another. However, its focus on family helps to make Kramer vs. Kramer one of the best movies of the 1970s.
Stepmom
While not a perfect movie, there is much to enjoy in the 1998 film Stepmom. The film takes a complex eye to changing ideas of what makes up a family, telling the story of two women navigating their place in looking after a pair of children.
Susan Sarandon plays Jackie Harrison, a divorced mother who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness. To complicate her life further, as she attempts to co-parent her two children along with her ex-husband, Luke's new girlfriend, Julia Roberts' Isabel, moves in and creates a whole new dynamic within the family.
Balancing ideas about parenting and caretaking, the film takes some surprisingly thoughtful turns, even if it occasionally leans a little saccharine. With great performances at its core, it remains an excellent film.
Is This Thing On?
An unusually interesting look at processing the dissolution of a relationship, Bradley Cooper's Is This Thing On? centers on the dynamics between Will Arnett's Alex and Laura Dern's Tess. Married long ago, and now in their forties, each reckons with the fact that they have given up things for their dynamic and to raise children together.
Their split is not bitter, and the two move on to a new phase in each of their lives. Tess dedicates herself to coaching, while Alex turns to the world of stand-up comedy, which helps to process how he really feels about his life and his relationships.
A complex look at marriage and divorce, Is This Thing On? brings a unique lens to a complicated subject, and creates something that feels both honest and genuinely thoughtful.
Crazy, Stupid, Love
Crazy, Stupid, Love is a compelling and smart romantic comedy that is full of fantastic stars. Steve Carell plays the central role of Cal, a middle-aged man whose wife asks him for a divorce. Unprepared for these events, he is helped by Jacob, an attractive and charismatic younger man played by Ryan Gosling, to meet women.
Of course, things quickly get messy. Jacob meets and falls in love with Emma Stone's Hannah, who turns out to be Cal's daughter. The dynamics become confused, and real questions about relationships, lifestyles, and suitability for partnership come to the fore.
Crazy, Stupid, Love confronts some real concerns about attraction, relationships, and showing up for one another. The script is genuinely funny and charming, and the characters are excellent.
Mrs. Doubtfire
One of the strongest movies that defined Robin Williams' career, Mrs. Doubtfire is a fantastic comedy that hinges on a stunningly charismatic performance. The film centers around Daniel Hillard, who, after his wife files for divorce, finds himself losing custody of his children until he is able to find and maintain a steady job.
In response, Daniel launches a scheme that is silly, but full of heart. He disguises himself as Euphegenia Doubtfire and takes on a job in his family home as a nanny. This affords him the opportunity to maintain a relationship with his children while also working a second job at a TV station.
The premise is a bit outsized and silly, but the execution is what makes the movie so strong. Williams balances comedy and real emotion as both Daniel and Mrs. Doubtfire, allowing the heavy subject matter of the film to be even more effective.
The Awful Truth (1937)
A silly, screwball comedy from the 1930s, The Awful Truth is an amusing story about a couple who enter into proceedings for divorce. There is a 90-day waiting period to process it, and in the meantime, each of the two pursues other romantic connections.
Still, neither seems to be able to let go of the other, and is unwilling to see them with anyone else. Cary Grant's Jerry and Irene Dunne's Lucy sabotage each other's new relationships at every turn, resulting in some excellent humor.
The stars had great chemistry, and the film relied heavily on their shared charisma as well as improvisation. It remains one of the best romantic comedies in the history of classic Hollywood.

item.description: TBC has been named the Best Corporate Bank by Euromoney for the third time, becoming the only bank from Georgia to receive the prestigious award in this category on three occasions. The recognition from the international financial publication further underscores TBC’s leading position in Georgia’s corporate banking market, where the bank holds a 43% share of corporate lending. Euromoney recognized TBC for its strong performance, innovation, digital transformation, and customer-centric approach.
item.content:encoded:
TBC has been named the Best Corporate Bank by Euromoney for the third time, becoming the only bank from Georgia to receive the prestigious award in this category on three occasions.
The recognition from the international financial publication further underscores TBC’s leading position in Georgia’s corporate banking market, where the bank holds a 43% share of corporate lending.
Euromoney recognized TBC for its strong performance, innovation, digital transformation, and customer-centric approach. By adopting advanced technologies, TBC is simplifying business processes for its corporate clients, providing faster and more seamless services, and supporting business continuity.
In 2025, TBC introduced artificial intelligence tools into its corporate banking operating model, including AI Analyst Copilot, which automated the preparation of credit documentation. Combined with process improvements, the use of AI contributed to an 11% year-on-year reduction in the time required to provide financing.
TBC also introduced an online foreign-currency trading module, enabling customers to agree on exchange rates and execute transactions in real time through internet and mobile banking. These enhancements have increased operational efficiency and further improved the customer experience.
The development of TBC’s Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system has also enabled the bank to create offers that are more closely tailored to the needs of individual businesses. As a result, 70% of business proposals have converted into new client relationships.
“We are proud that TBC has won the Euromoney award for Best Corporate Bank every time we have been nominated in this category. This is further recognition of our leading position in the corporate banking market. TBC ranks first in corporate deposits, lending, and trade finance. We serve more than 6,700 corporate customers, which means that some of the largest businesses in Georgia place their trust in TBC. The Euromoney award reflects the daily work of our team, our focus on innovation, and the long-term partnerships we build with our customers. By providing solutions tailored to businesses’ needs and creating an outstanding customer experience, we will continue to partner with the private sector and contribute to the development of Georgia’s economy,” said Meri Chachanidze, Director of Corporate Banking Business Management at TBC.

item.content:encoded:
Passionate Northampton fundraiser branches out to host crafters carousel workshop – think speed dating but with crafts
A passionate fundraiser in Northampton has branched out to host a new style of event called a crafters carousel workshop, which she has described as speed dating but with crafts.
Natalie Wood is known for organising charity events in memory of her late brother Sam Grove. These raise money and awareness for Northamptonshire Mind to support mental health and address the stigma around alcohol addiction.
Sam tragically passed away at the age of 30 in March 2023 and Natalie has organised multiple successful community events, including a winter shopping experience at The Elgar Centre and summer gatherings at The George Inn.
Natalie has now broadened her horizons to host events under the umbrella organisation of Natalie Wood Events, and the crafters carousel workshop is taking place from 10am until 1pm on October 18 at The Brampton Halt.
This will be a relaxed morning when attendees will get to try four different crafts with a brilliant group of makers. You will spend 30 minutes at each station before moving onto the next, and you do not need to consider yourself crafty to come along.
This is an introductory and experimental workshop, with a focus on simply having a go, trying something new and seeing what you enjoy.
The first station will be needle felting with Ali Edwards from Fuzzycrumbs, during which attendees will make a small pumpkin from 100 percent wool. The next is centred around essential oils and making your own roller ball with Sabrina Smart.
Kerry Mattock Tobin from Kerry’s Creative Therapeutic Workshops will help the crafters get hands on with clay, and Lizzie Foster from Hoglet House Crafts will be teaching the basics of paper quilling.
Because no morning of crafting is complete without refreshments, there will be cakes and drinks too. Tickets are £30 per person and include the four taster sessions, all the materials you need, your creations to take home, and the chance to try something outside of your comfort zone.
There will also be the opportunity to purchase some of the crafters’ kits to take away, so if you discover something you love, you can carry on creating at home. Spaces are limited so secure your ticket while they are still available.

item.title: [Dawn] Romance isn’t dead, but in Lahore, it is flatlining
item.dc:creator: Noor ur Rehman
item.description: Dating in Lahore is an entire sport in itself. item.content:encoded:
Dating in Lahore is an entire sport in itself. You have to pick the right coffee shop, the right corner, the right time of day, preferably somewhere your mother’s friend is unlikely to walk in, and pray the weather doesn’t ruin the outfit you spent an hour choosing.
Step inside any air-conditioned hipster café and you’ll spot them immediately. At least three couples tucked into corner booths, oblivious to the September heat, holding hands, or spoon-feeding each other tres leches cake while the staff desperately looks anywhere else.
Psychiatrist John Bowlby noted in his work on attachment theory that our drive for deep intimacy is a lot more than a nice-to-have. It’s an instinctual imperative. He observed that most intense human emotions are sparked during the formation, maintenance, and disruption of romantic bonds.
But it’s no secret that in Pakistan, instinctual imperative collides with cultural veto. Outside of a few ultra cosmopolitan bubble zones in Lahore, dating is policed by a rigid mix of religious norms and cultural scrutiny for consenting young adults.
To explore this weird, wonderful, and deeply neurotic dynamic, I polled 34 anonymous Lahoris navigating the city’s covert romance scene. I asked them two simple questions:
-
Is dating in Lahore difficult? Why?
-
How do you deal with the weight of secrecy, guilt, conservative judgment, or moral hesitation that may come with it?
Despite growing up on Bollywood’s grand declarations of love, rewatching all seasons of Friends, listening to Atif Aslam’s heartbreak anthems in a loop, and memorising Jaun Elia’s most devastating couplets, young Lahoris seem remarkably unprepared for romance in real life.
My anonymous survey confirmed it. Gen Z and millennials alike are largely paralysed by the prospect of modern romance.
A familiar tension kept surfacing across the responses I received. The inclination to date existed alongside a palpable fear of judgement and social consequences. Online discourse was cited as evidence; posts and reels on Instagram about dating can quickly become battlegrounds over what constitutes acceptable behaviour, with some commenters not merely disapproving of dating but calling for stricter boundaries in the name of moral values and “purity”. On the other side are those who defend the right to date, though often with a disclaimer attached: adults should be free to make their own choices, provided nobody is harmed. Even the defence of dating, then, is frequently framed as a case for personal freedom as opposed to an embrace of romance.
The Gen Z and millennials have been subjected to relentless messaging from both progressive and traditional benches, which puts dating at an intriguing intersection of two irreconcilable realities. Modern psychology and liberal education tells them to set boundaries and be the CEO of their own love life. Pakistani family culture tells them those boundaries are a sin. Caught in the crossfire, Lahoris are perpetually oscillating between self-actualisation and filial duty, paying the emotional tax of whichever voice screams the loudest.
To the traditionalists, any line crossed between men and women—whether a fleeting friendship or a casual date (what some would call a situationship these days)—is tagged as a moral liability. According to them, the rise in domestic violence, messy divorces, and infidelity traces straight back to liberal schooling, the lawless noise of social media, and the erasure of gender boundaries.
Flip the coin, and the progressives see the exact same horrors. The abuse, the fractured marriages, the betrayal, and the senseless murder of women, as the grim byproduct of missing liberal values and a culture that starves men and women of normal, healthy dialogue.
But even in the polished pockets of Lahore where dating is rather normalised, the reality on the ground isn’t as straightforward. Anonymised accounts from those who have dated/are currently dating in the city, noted a sense of inherent paranoia. On the streets, it’s a constant dodge of prying eyes and predatory police. Inside the hip cafes, the romantic mood competes with the cold sting of overpriced Spanish lattes and fettuccine.
The anxieties of modern dating take different shapes depending on who you ask. For women, the stakes scale up drastically. A single slip-up, a spotted outing by a relative, jeopardises their access to education, career, and in many cases, basic mobility. One woman shared her fear of being doxxed wherein her intimate photos and private texts could be weaponised across social media. Another admitted to fearing that a bitter ex might resurface after marriage to destroy her future. A segment of women answered that they constantly grapple with ingrained religious guilt. For most though, the core fear was far more immediate. It was confronting the entrenched patriarchal mindsets of their own families, where dating risked public dishonour.
For young couples, a simple moment of holding hands in a parked car carries the threat of police shakedowns and extortion. Worse still, the constant stream of news headlines reporting violence against dating partners leaves many terrified of the very people they are meeting. When things turn dangerous, the closeted nature of these relationships cuts off all escape routes.
As always, the heaviest burden falls on women, who face a court of public opinion and a legal apparatus far quicker to condemn a female victim than her male counterpart, a double standard laid bare on social feeds after every fresh report of abuse or femicide.
And yet, across Lahore, people continue to risk their safety, reputations, and futures for love, intimacy, or basic connection. Whatever one’s moral stance on the practice, dating in this context is a privilege for a few, a calculated risk for many, and an outright liability for most. Still, against all odds and taboos, the daring spirit for human attachment remains.
The views expressed in Prism Reflections are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial policy of Dawn.
Prism Reflections is a space for voices and experiences that shape, and are shaped by, Pakistan’s defining news stories. Do you have a personal story that intersects with the news? Send it to prism@dawn.com.

item.title: [The Mercury News] Dear Abby: My son says my generosity is cutting into his inheritance
item.dc:creator: Abigail Van Buren
item.description: DEAR ABBY: I have three grown children. One son, “Charles,” with his wife and three elementary-school-aged children, rents the house next door to me for about $1,200 a month less than I might charge a non-family renter. My other two kids live hundreds of miles away. My younger son, “James,” is unmarried and without children. He thinks I’m being unfair to him and his sister because I’m not charging the maximum rent the house might get, thereby reducing his inheritance. I place great value in havi
item.content:encoded:
DEAR ABBY: I have three grown children. One son, “Charles,” with his wife and three elementary-school-aged children, rents the house next door to me for about $1,200 a month less than I might charge a non-family renter. My other two kids live hundreds of miles away.
My younger son, “James,” is unmarried and without children. He thinks I’m being unfair to him and his sister because I’m not charging the maximum rent the house might get, thereby reducing his inheritance.
I place great value in having Charles and his family living next door to me. James thinks I should be regularly compensating him and his sister for what he claims I’m giving to Charles and his family. What do you think?
— LANDLORD DAD
DEAR LANDLORD DAD: I think it’s presumptuous and ill-mannered of your younger son to count his inheritance while his father is still living and breathing.
Charles’ rent is between you and him, and frankly, James shouldn’t be privy to the details of the arrangement. Tell your grasping younger son that every time he brings this up in the future, you’ll deduct $1,200 from his share of the estate and divide it between Charles and his sister.
DEAR ABBY: You sometimes ask readers to share their pet peeves. I am a public school teacher, and here is mine: Parents wonder why their children misbehave, argue with them and act out with attention-getting behaviors. My advice to them: Put down those cellphones and pay attention to your kids!
I just had a conference with a mother whose children argue, pout and scream when they are told to do something at home. These children have no special needs and don’t demonstrate those behaviors at school. Abby, the woman texted on her phone throughout the meeting. That behavior is not OK.
The next time I encounter a parent who does it, I will ask the person if he or she would like to suspend the conference to take care of the pressing business. Perhaps these parents need to be embarrassed a bit so they will realize how inappropriate texting or talking on the phone is when face-to-face with another person.
— A VENTING EDUCATOR
DEAR EDUCATOR: I agree that what the parent did was extremely rude. It sent the unmistakable message that not only was the meeting not important to her, but neither was anything you had to say.
If you are asking me for permission to inform parents that cellphones must be silenced and out of sight during conferences with you, you have it. My advice is to say it as soon as the parent enters your classroom. You can frame it as parents following the same rules as students in your space.
DEAR ABBY: I have two daughters, ages 19 and 21. They both have jobs. My husband and I would like them to help pay for our family vacation because they expect expensive experiences. Are we wrong to ask them to contribute?
— HELPING OUT IN NEW YORK
DEAR HELPING: I don’t think it would be wrong to enlighten your daughters about what the family vacation is costing. If their expectations will uncomfortably strain your budget, explain that you will need them to chip in so they can experience everything they want.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips wrote this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.content:encoded:
Your Weekly Love Horoscope for The Week of September 21, 2026. Discover your Weekly Love Horoscope for each zodiac sign here.
Aries
What does your family know about romance? A lot, actually. They might not be the first people you'd think to ask for advice, but consider doing so on Monday. They would probably be flattered by your interest in their perspective. On Tuesday and Wednesday, you're going to learn a few new things on your own. They're great, very romantic days that most likely end with smooching. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday return you to the ordinary world of working, exercising, errands, but a phone call on Sunday to you-know-who would go over smashingly.
Taurus
Thursday, Friday, and Saturday (fun days already, generally speaking) have the added magic of being particularly romantic. Monday? Not so much. It's not a bad day. You'll probably eat some delicious things and have fun in social settings. It's just not romantic. Tuesday and Wednesday are outright annoying, featuring encounters with people who want things they aren't able to articulate. But Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are very different. Blossoms figure in the stars, which is appropriate metaphorically. On Sunday, you have a spring in your step.
Gemini
The end of this week, Sunday, to be exact, is romantic. Sunday is a blast. Sunday gives you the opportunity to focus exclusively on you-know-who, and when you focus on someone, you dazzle like no one else can. Put all your eggs into the basket that is Sunday, because the rest of the week is kind of generic. Monday is a classic Monday: hazy, stressful. Tuesday and Wednesday are fun enough, crowded with like-minded people, and you get good ideas, but nothing happens that has the frisson of love. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are bogged down by family. But then there's Sunday. Wonderful, action-packed, heart-fluttering Sunday!
Cancer
Though you're not particularly disposed to romance this week, Monday is a perfect day for new beginnings. If you're single, it's time to flirt with you-know-who. It's a good day to be assertive. Tuesday and Wednesday find you making a purchase with the future in mind, possibly by yourself, possibly with someone (perhaps a romantic partner). Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are better for cleaning the house than for painting the town, but cleaning the house can be fun (in a dorky way). Sunday is less fun. The house may be clean, but something's out of order. You'll figure it out.
Leo
If you're single, this isn't the week that's going to change that (except maybe on Sunday). But if you already have someone special, this week is bliss. Monday is sweet and calming, the kind of day when you feel like sitting under a tree with someone and drinking tea. On Tuesday and Wednesday, you're glowing from within. Everyone is showering you with praise. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are mundane by comparison. You're surrounded by yellow pads full of scribbling about the future, financial projections...stuff like that. Sunday is straight out of a romance novel. In a good way.
Prepare yourself to take on each month with your personalized Monthly Horoscope!
Virgo
You have a talent for doing things on your own and doing them better than someone with an army of assistants could do. But not on Monday. You could use a couple of assistants on Monday. Or at least a few friends standing on the sidelines and giving you advice. It's not a particularly romantic week, but if you get done what you hope to, you're going to become practically famous, which could bode well for your romantic future. It's true that your happiness often directly corresponds to the extent to which people want to be around you. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are particularly happy days.
Libra
This is a healing week for you, bringing your innermost thoughts to the surface. This isn't easy, so give yourself the quiet solitude you need in order to process them. You could be feeling more sensitive than usual, and it might be harder to clearly express how you're feeling. If you have something important to say to a lover, give yourself the time to find the right words. Midweek is a beautiful time to truly feel your feelings. The good, the bad, and the ugly. By week's end, you'll encounter an incredibly forgiving moment, helping you treat yourself with compassion as you embark on a new chapter.
Scorpio
Your dreams are hard to fathom on Monday. What could your subconscious be telling you? And what does it have to do with your love life? Good questions. This week offers little in the way of answers. A fight with your boss could well take place on Tuesday or Wednesday, but Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are mellow, though not without flashes of excitement. A friend has been keeping something from you and they're finally going to spill it. Exciting! If you have a secret to confess, now is the time. Nothing new happens on the romance front on Sunday, but it's an easy, pleasant day.
Sagittarius
It's entirely possible that you and you-know-who are right for each other, but it doesn't seem like it on Monday. Mismatched energies are confusing everything. You don't want to go out...your love interest does...then you both change your minds. Stay in. On Tuesday and Wednesday, travel is in the stars. Whether it's a trip down the highway or through the clouds, it goes well. On Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, other people are once again making you nuts (even people you love), but on Sunday, you're reminded of what you see in them.
Capricorn
You and you-know-who are in the middle of a disagreement on Monday, and nothing you say seems to make it any better. It's likely that they're overreacting. Then again, you're not the best judge. Expect extremes in energy and almost nothing in the way of romance on Tuesday and Wednesday. A difference of opinion at work might lead to outright bickering. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are the highlight of the week, what with you connecting with old friends and getting tons done, but you probably won't end up snuggling on the couch with anyone. Sunday is perfect for a fresh, new start.
Aquarius
You're feeling very sensitive on Monday, which isn't always the best thing when it comes to your romantic life. It can confuse issues. It can create issues where there aren't any. Stop thinking so much and go where your natural energy leads. Tuesday and Wednesday are relationship oriented. Compromise, flexibility, and extraordinary connections figure strongly. But on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, the romantic content of your life is overshadowed by business (or at least financial) matters. Sunday would be a good time to call you-know-who just to chat.
Pisces
You put on a fun love song and dance around your house in your underwear on Monday. Or at least you do this in your mind. Monday is one of those super fun romantic days. On Tuesday and Wednesday, you're doing more serious forms of exercise than dancing in your underwear (it's a shame that can't be your sole way of keeping fit!), but on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, you're not in a very active mood. Your current relationship has hit a snag, and you two have to talk it through. Sunday has you wondering if it's going to work out.
What does your moon sign mean? Learn more about your emotional world with a Moon Sign Reading! 🌙

item.title: [InDaily Queensland] Manly Boathouse, love-bombing and finding her voice – Lottie McLeod on her latest EP
