item.content:encoded:
“Micro cheating” is a bit slippery to define. In my parents’ day, in the 1980s, I imagine it would be removing your wedding ring when you attended a drinks party. Or failing to mention that you have a husband when someone offers to buy you a baby-cham at the bar. Nowadays there are many ways to micro-cheat with WhatsApp and social media, making it easier than ever.
A term popularised by the dating coach Melanie Schilling in 2017, micro cheating isn’t a one size fits all. What does and doesn’t count feels individual and varies between couples (is liking someone else’ s Instagram photos micro cheating?) I’d personally define it as the things you do or say which you know would upset your partner if they knew. A survey found 40 per cent of Brits believe that “developing any romantic feelings [even] without acting on them” is cheating. So perhaps calling it “micro” is just an attempt to make it sound less terrible than it really is.
The problem is: I think if most married couples were honest, they’d admit that they’ve thought that way about other people, and fantasised about sleeping with them. I’m not proud of it but I have been micro-cheating on my husband for 18 months.
Shorts
I’m 48 and have been married to Simon* for 22 years. We have two teenage boys. Simon is wedded to his work and we get on well, but I feel like we’re ships in the night. We spend too long on our laptops. We talk about how we need to prioritise one another but we’re too busy. We have stressful jobs, and at the end of the day, we tend to stare at our phones. Perimenopause hasn’t helped much either. I don’t fancy Simon and feel angry a lot.
A year and a half ago, I met Dean at a health and wellness conference in Corfu. I work in corporate hospitality and we were staying at a beautiful luxury hotel. Each day we’d attend talks about the ‘future of hospitality’, which was boring, but at 5pm everyone would meet for drinks.
On the second night of the conference, Dean and I ended up sitting together at the local taverna. He was Irish, in his late 40s, recently divorced and worked in PR. He lived in Bali, not the UK. I remember noticing him right away; he was good-looking, but I also dismissed him as annoying. He kept name-dropping famous people that he’d worked with.
Then after a while, perhaps influenced by three glasses of wine, we got chatting. We had a lot in common. We loved 90s dance music. We’d gone clubbing to the same places in our youth. We loved the same films – any Steve Martin comedy. I realised that talking about this stuff was something I missed. Simon and I were in functional parent mode; we talked about what to eat for tea and whether the boys were going to fail their exams.
Dean and I got drunk and we swapped numbers. I felt 18, like I was in this fantasy where I was desirable again. To be honest, I didn’t think I fancied people anymore until I met Dean.
When I woke up the following day, I felt guilty. Why had I found it so easy to give Dean my number? I told myself he would be a “useful work contact”, and vowed to give him a wide berth. On the second night, however, when I was sitting at the bar, quite drunk yet again (I was letting my hair down; I might even have been smoking too…), I got a text from Dean. “I was hoping we could meet up. Fancy coming to my room for a nightcap?”
To be honest, I was stunned. I’d not seen him all day and thought he’d been flirting with me the night before because a lot of people in our industry can be super friendly. I told him that I’d give it a miss. Then he sent another text saying he was disappointed – “I thought we had chemistry,” he said.
At that point I should have fully shut it down but instead I typed: “I really like you. I would love to come to your room but I can’t do it as I know what will happen. I’m sorry.” The reality was that because I was away on my own, in a different country, I felt like I should have a holiday fling!
I fell asleep and the next day got a text from Dean saying that he was leaving early as he had to go home for a work meeting. I felt flat, like I’d missed an opportunity. If I’d slept with Dean, then probably the whole thing would have finished right there. But instead, that’s when we started messaging one another in earnest.
We used Instagram messenger, not WhatsApp – where I text most people. I’ve never actually texted a man who wasn’t Simon, not romantically at least and to begin with I was disoriented. Sometimes Dean would text about work-related things. So he’d be sharing a client and then he would be telling me that he was feeling sad because he’d injured his knee.
He would send me selfies and photos of everything in his life. Not naked ones, but just a diary showing what he was doing. We messaged a lot. It was a running conversation that we picked up as soon as we were both online. I started putting kisses at the end of each message. I also confided in him about feeling lonely.
It felt like cheating because I don’t usually put kisses at the end of messages. Also, I was finding that Dean was cropping up more often in my mind, and I’d wonder what he was up to. But he was also so far away that it felt safe. We didn’t have to take anything further, and Simon didn’t have to find out.
At other times I convinced myself it wasn’t cheating as Dean would share information about a woman he was seeing. Weirdly, I felt hurt but knew I couldn’t – I’m married!
The life that Dean was living seemed idyllic and a long way away from me putting washing in the machine and avoiding Simon, who was often in a permanent sulk. I should have felt guiltier, but as the weeks passed, I justified it because I was feeling low. Our marriage had deteriorated. I was comparing Simon to Dean and Dean was just a fantasy. But it felt strangely intimate too. He’d share songs that we both loved. I found myself getting obsessive. I knew it was ridiculous. Months passed and each morning I’d wait for a message, feeling disappointed if there was nothing there.
Simon was now working every hour of the day; I mean, I assumed he was. I would regularly delete the chats with Dean but Simon has never been one to check my phone. One time my son Aidan picked it up and I hadn’t deleted the conversation. He said: “Who is this dude?” I blushed. “He’s just a work friend. We message about work stuff,” I’d said. Luckily, he didn’t mention it again.
When I spoke to female friends, they were aghast. Why was I bothering to text this guy who lived so far away? What was his agenda? Money? Did he have any intention of meeting up with me? What was I getting out of the whole thing? It was hard to explain. I was getting friendship, and a bit of flirtation thrown in for good measure.
With micro-cheating, you get “micro-doses” of guilt. I justified it because I was bored. Because Simon and I didn’t have sex. Because I felt old and like time was running out. The truth was that I felt closer to Dean than to Simon after 12 months of texting. We knew each other really well.
He would often say things like “if we’d met back in the 90s, we would have been an item.” But he never made plans to come to the UK, even though I knew that he could. There were times when I tried to push things, suggesting that perhaps I should come to Bali. I increasingly felt like my feelings were much stronger than his.
Then one morning a couple of months ago, when I was getting ready to drive to the garden centre, I checked my phone and Dean had sent me a photo of his penis! I felt like perhaps he’d sent it by mistake. Luckily, it disappeared as Instagram has a one-view feature. “I’m sorry,” Dean texted later. I felt so mixed about it. I did fancy him. I sometimes thought about what it would be like. I dreamt about it, in fact.
The photo did feel like a line had been crossed. I also felt like he was maybe playing me; if I didn’t message for a few days, he’d double down and send me a long voice note. I’d hear his voice, immediately felt closer and more obsessive again.
But the photo made me decide to go cold turkey. I blocked him – of course there was no resolution because we didn’t have a relationship in the first place but I felt like I was going mad. Then, after two weeks, I unblocked him and messaged. “I can’t stop thinking about you. How’s work?” I knew it was stupid. That was last month.
I know I have to put energy into my marriage but I feel so over it. The energy I get from Dean makes me feel alive. Today I am still “micro cheating”. Except it doesn’t feel quite so micro anymore. It feels like a massive lie because it’s been going on so long. I keep telling myself it’s pointless. That I am betraying Simon. That I owe it to my sons to give it up and make more of an effort at home. There are days when I feel Dean and I will meet up in real life and others when I think he’s stringing a whole host of women along.
He’s an enigma in many ways. The opposite of the man I’ve shared a bed with for so many years. I know that I’m wasting time. But I’m also totally addicted. I sometimes daydream a scenario where we meet. I also know that if we did meet, there’d be too much pressure on the whole thing, as my expectations of him are way too high. I have sort of made him into an ideal partner, filled in the blanks and ensured he has all the things I look for. He’d never be able to live up to that high standard anyway.

item.content:encoded:
Dear Abby | Good neighbor learns inclusivity has limits
Today's advice from Dear Abby.
DEAR ABBY: I am a single woman in a friendly neighborhood. Every month, I have the neighbors over for dinner and a movie. I like to be inclusive — bring the kids, bring the dogs! One couple recently had their elderly mom move in, and I installed a ramp so she could join us. Babies cry, dogs bark, women breastfeed, but all are welcome. I put sleeping bags on the floor for the kids to sit on while grownups sit on the couches. Cleanup is a bear, but every squished meatball on the floor reminds me how much I love everyone.
Recently, a new couple moved in, so of course I invited them and their 6-year-old to join us. They warned me that he has severe autism, but I told them everyone is welcome, that he wouldn’t be expected to be quiet and that the house is thoroughly kid-proofed. When the family showed up to join us, their child was horrible, even by my nonexistent standards for kiddo behavior. He screamed, threw food, bit, spit and hit the other kids and the dogs for an hour. Finally, everyone started to leave before the movie was over. The boy’s parents really did try their best, and I was genuinely sympathetic. They apologized the next day and said that if they were welcome in the future, they would alternate one parent staying home with their son while the other joined us. That sounds reasonable, but I don’t like it. I can’t be inclusive just when it suits me. They have since invited me to their home for dinner, and their son was just as bad there, banishing my thoughts that maybe it was just a strange house he was reacting to. I don’t know what to do with all this. I’m looking for a magic wand. Any suggestions?
— NEIGHBORLY IN THE EAST
DEAR NEIGHBORLY: You are a caring, lovely person, but there is no magic wand that will make that child’s severe autism and behavior problems go away. Because you are determined to entertain the entire family, the practical solution would be to invite them and their son over on another evening when other children and pets won’t be at risk of injury. Your movie night will be history if it is disrupted like that again. While I commend you for wanting to befriend the family, I think the parents had the right solution.
** ** **
DEAR ABBY: I’m 70 now, and many of my friends and family spend our time together complaining about their various ailments. I, too, have had some problems but do not make them a part of our visits unless I’m asked about them. How can I rethink how to make these times more positive for everyone involved?
— POSITIVE IN OREGON
DEAR POSITIVE: Sometimes, people of a certain age talk about their health problems because they have become less active and can find little else to talk about. To keep the energy flowing in a more positive direction, help your friends find hobbies and other interests to discuss. Even if they have medical issues, most people can manage quiet activities like board games, card games, a book club or a knitting circle. If all else fails, you can always ask them about their families as a change of subject.

Singles may meet someone through friends, gatherings, or shared interests, while couples can reconnect by making time for laughter and enjoyable experiences together. item.content:encoded:
Love feels more social and joyful this week. Singles may meet someone through friends, gatherings, or shared interests, while couples can reconnect by making time for laughter and enjoyable experiences together. Let romance feel lighter rather than turning every moment into a serious discussion.
Weekly Love Horoscope, September 21 to September 27, 2026: Romantic clarity may shape your emotional journey this week
Weekly Love Horoscope, September 21 to September 27, 2026. Find what these predictions have in store for you.
Love Tip: Make space for fun and genuine companionship.
Crystal Remedy: Carnelian: Carry it during social outings to encourage confidence, warmth, and openness.
Emotional maturity becomes important in relationships. You may need to respond calmly to a sensitive situation rather than reacting immediately. Singles could be attracted to someone emotionally grounded and dependable.
Love Tip: Express your feelings without allowing them to control your response.
Crystal Remedy: Amazonite: Keep it close during important conversations to encourage balanced communication.
Romantic uncertainty may leave you questioning someone's intentions. Avoid filling gaps in communication with assumptions. Singles should take time to understand a new connection, while couples may benefit from discussing concerns directly.
Love Tip: Look for clarity instead of creating your own answers.
Crystal Remedy: Fluorite: Place it near your bedside to encourage clear thinking and emotional discernment.
A strong sense of mutual affection can develop this week. Singles may encounter someone who seems genuinely receptive, while couples can strengthen their bond through honest conversations and shared plans.
Love Tip: Meet each other halfway instead of expecting one person to carry the relationship.
Crystal Remedy: Rhodonite: Carry it as a reminder of compassion, reciprocity, and emotional balance.
A fresh romantic chapter may be calling you. Singles could feel drawn toward an unexpected connection, while couples may benefit from trying something new together. Don't let fear of uncertainty prevent you from experiencing something different.
Love Tip: Take a romantic chance without abandoning your boundaries.
Crystal Remedy: Sunstone: Keep it with you on dates or social occasions to encourage confidence and positive energy.
A sweet message, unexpected attraction, or emotionally refreshing moment could brighten your week. Singles may discover interest through a gentle interaction, while couples can benefit from expressing affection more openly.
Love Tip: Pay attention to small gestures; they can reveal genuine interest.
Crystal Remedy: Pink Opal: Keep it near your personal space to encourage tenderness and emotional openness.
You may seek greater stability and clarity in love. Established relationships could focus on commitment, shared values, or future plans. Singles may be drawn toward someone whose intentions feel serious rather than uncertain.
Love Tip: Choose relationships that respect your values and boundaries.
Crystal Remedy: Howlite: Keep it beside your bed to encourage calm communication and thoughtful choices.
You may want greater control or certainty within your romantic life. Healthy boundaries are useful, but avoid becoming overly controlling when emotions feel uncertain. Singles can benefit from being confident about what they want without trying to force an outcome.
Love Tip: Lead with confidence, not control.
Crystal Remedy: Tiger Eye: Carry it when you need confidence while maintaining emotional balance.
You may feel emotionally tired but still hopeful about love. If you've been through repeated disappointments, this week asks you to protect your heart without completely closing it. Couples may need patience while working through a lingering issue.
Love Tip: Protect your energy while leaving room for genuine connection.
Crystal Remedy: Red Jasper: Keep it close when you need grounding, resilience, and emotional steadiness.
Romantic boundaries may need strengthening. Someone could challenge your position or make you question what you truly want. Singles should avoid chasing validation, while couples can strengthen trust by standing up for their needs respectfully.
Love Tip: Don't compromise your core needs just to maintain harmony.
Crystal Remedy: Black Tourmaline: Keep it near your personal space as a reminder to maintain healthy emotional boundaries.
The past may return through a message, meeting, or unexpected reminder. A familiar connection could bring warmth, but ask yourself whether it belongs in your present or simply carries sentimental value.
Love Tip: Let nostalgia inform you without allowing it to make the decision for you.
Crystal Remedy: Aquamarine: Carry it when revisiting old connections to encourage emotional clarity and calm.
Love takes on a more serious and secure tone. Couples may discuss family, long-term plans, or building a stronger future together. Singles may be attracted to someone who offers stability and genuine commitment.
Love Tip: Look for consistency that can support a lasting relationship.
Crystal Remedy: Green Jade: Keep it in your bedroom or carry it to symbolize harmony, stability, and enduring affection.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Sunday, September 20: That Conversation Won't Wait Much Longer
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for September 20, 2026. The Capricorn Moon squares Mercury in Libra on Sunday, encouraging you to ask for what you need in your love life.
This energy is all about emotional reassurance. To feel confident in your relationship, you need to know your feelings are reciprocated. Rather than guessing how the other person feels, ask. If you want to know if they love you, this is the day to find out. If you’re hoping to talk about the future, it’s time to bring up that conversation. No matter where you stand in your relationship, it’s better to know for sure.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Sunday, September 20, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be clear on your reasons, Aries. While you're searching for genuine love, you must be mindful of your reasons. This means that despite your desire for love or connection, you may also be looking for validation in your relationship.
Honor this very human need to know that you and your partner both value this connection. On Sunday, ask them how they feel. This will help you have the clarity you need and feel more secure in the future.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Honor your need for emotional safety, Taurus. Love is always a risk; however, that doesn’t mean you should take a chance without the knowledge to back it up.
Before you take a leap of faith, make sure the person you’re leaping with is going to do the same. On Sunday, don’t be afraid to talk about what you imagine your life will look like together, or the kinds of changes you’re both craving. This will help you feel confident that the only risk you’re taking is a new beginning together.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t be afraid to talk it out, Gemini. Talking is one of your strengths, but you must make sure you’re saying what really matters on Sunday.
Instead of focusing on the fun and beautiful bits of a life together, get down to the nitty-gritty that actually defines a relationship. Whether this includes financial matters or your emotional needs, the more real you get, the better you will feel about where this connection is headed.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You deserve the love and life you’re dreaming of, Cancer. That includes the home and family, but you must make sure your partner is on the same page as you.
On Sunday, ask the hard questions and genuinely listen to their answers. It may be tempting to think they’ll change their mind eventually or that this will work itself out, but you need to prioritize truth over feelings right now.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Create your own sense of inner safety, Leo. While a relationship should be your safe place in the world, it’s not your partner's responsibility to make you feel safe. You have to be willing to do some of that work on your own.
Learn to trust yourself and provide what you need. This will help you receive a healthy partner and not make them feel like they're carrying the weight of the relationship.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You deserve to be valued, Virgo. That means your partner sees you for all that you are. They don’t take you for granted or dismiss your unique energy as something they can receive from just anyone.
Yet that doesn’t mean you’ve been feeling this way. On Sunday, bring up how you’ve been feeling and what you need. This situation won't resolve itself on its own.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Design the life you want, Libra. As much as your zodiac sign represents partnership, you must create the life you want to live for yourself. You can’t give up your dreams or needs in an effort to fake intimacy in a relationship.
On Sunday, be sure you’re prioritizing your desires, especially those involving home or emotional safety. Don't wait for your love interest or partner to do it for you.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Let yourself be seen for all you are, Scorpio. You don’t have to hide your darkness to be loved. In the early stages of relationships, you often try to come across as lighter than you really are. This can mean gaslighting yourself about what you’ve been through or even survived, but that’s not what genuine love is based on.
On Sunday, choose to reveal your most authentic self and be honest about who you are. That is the only way to receive what you truly deserve.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your independence can make a relationship stronger, Sagittarius. You deserve to be financially stable on your own, yet that doesn’t mean that you can’t enjoy greater success with the right partner.
On Sunday, find a new balance in how you approach independence and partnership. Cultivate your own independence, but stay open to the idea that the right person can help further your dreams of financial wealth and abundance.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Ask for what you need, Capricorn. Speaking up isn’t always your forte, as you tend to be the strong and silent type. However, you should not hold back on Sunday.
Honor what you’re seeking from your partner, whether it’s validation for where the relationship is headed or interest in a newer connection. Asking for what you need is a core part of you actually receiving it.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Give yourself the confirmation you need, Aquarius. While you may be seeking validation that you’re headed in the right direction, only you can give that to yourself.
On Sunday, meditate or talk to your spirit guides. Right now, you need divine confirmation, which means you must create time to connect with that part of yourself.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Lean on those you love, Pisces. You aren’t alone, no matter how much that inner voice tries to convince you otherwise. On Sunday, open up to those closest to you and let them support you through this time of transition.
Reach out to your friends and loved ones. Be honest with how you’re feeling and what is going on in your life. This will help you make the right choice in your romantic life and affirm that you really are being supported.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.dc:creator: Neeraj Dhankher

item.content:encoded:
There will be a desire to enter into relationships without the burden of unnecessary emotional stress. There will be a sense of confidence and attraction. Your Moon is in Sagittarius and Purva Ashadha Nakshatra. You are full of conviction and passion. Single people may feel more confident in their search for a romantic partner. There may be more candour between couples about plans for the future, their feelings or shared experiences.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
Enjoy the lighter side of love, but don't discount others' feelings. Purva Ashadha can make one strongly believe in their own view and can lead to stubborn disagreements if neither side listens. Couples are encouraged to spend time doing leisure activities, travelling or new experiences. Singles can be attracted to energetic people, but it is important to see whether the attraction remains when the initial excitement fades. The most powerful confidence is that which is accompanied by respect and patience.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Gemini: You may find yourself with too many romantic options, or you may get mixed signals. Be sure you know what you really want before you commit to it.
Choosing the simpler options might help you out of your emotional confusion.
Virgo: You may focus too much on the practical shortcomings of someone who otherwise suits your personality. Let the connection develop before you decide whether small differences matter.
Pisces: Your current partner might be acting more independent than you'd like. Don’t interpret their desire for independence as an emotional retreat. Where expectations are less constraining, trust could be enhanced.
Cancer: You may be seeking comfort, while a close relative is looking for adventure or change. Don't take this difference personally.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Scorpio: Your vulnerability is natural and can create a romantic magnetism of great intensity. Singles can connect through shared interests, social events, learning or travel. Disrupt their routines and get couples to rekindle their sense of excitement.
Aries: Your self-confidence could be just what it takes to move a romance forward. A direct invitation, an impromptu plan or an obvious sign of attraction can prompt an encouraging response.
Leo: Your warmth and charm work in your favor. Someone may be more receptive to your advances. The existing relationships can be more playful and loving.
Libra: A romantic opportunity may arise from a social interaction. Your easygoing attitude can help keep the conversation flowing, especially when you’re talking to someone who loves culture, travel, or creative things.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Taurus: Slow changes in steady romance.
Scorpio:
There can be strong feelings, but emotional control can help, and there’s no need for unnecessary tension.
Capricorn: Personal obligations may limit leisure time, but affection is consistent.
Aquarius: A friendship could turn romantic, but there’s no need to put a label on it just yet.
Lucky Action of the Day
Shared enthusiasm can be a spark for attraction and a help for conversation.

item.dc:creator: Susan Lochrie
item.description: A FORMER St Columba's High pupil who is now travelling the world after learning to love languages at school returned to the classroom to inspire a new generation. item.content:encoded:
A FORMER St Columba's High pupil who is now travelling the world after learning to love languages at school returned to the classroom to inspire a new generation.
Anna Gibson, 24, told a group of students how opportunities have opened up for her after falling in love with both French and Spanish in secondary.
She went on to study the languages at university and, after living in Spain and Paris for two years, she is now heading for the Pacific island of Tahiti to teach English.
Anna was invited to back to the Gourock school by Modern languages principal Emma Donnelly to share her experiences and demonstrate how modern languages can impact career opportunities.
The Wemyss Bay woman said: "I have no background in languages at home or anything. When I started secondary I thought I would go down the science and engineering route.
"But I loved learning languages, I learned Spanish first then French. It was my passion and I was so encouraged by Emma and the teachers here. They are so supportive.
"I decided to go for it and do languages at Glasgow University, my parents were supportive and just said do what you love.
"I have never looked back since. I loved uni, I took every opportunity that came my way.
"I ended up teaching in France, I worked in Spain and then I went to live in Paris was two years. I have never said no to any opportunity.
"I am now going to teach English in Tahiti. I never thought imagined this would be my life. It is a dream come true.
"I think it is so important that young people like me know the doors that can open for you if you learn and speak another language."
Anna said: "When you speak the language of a country you understand the culture and the mindset, it unlocks so much more."
Her experiences had a massive impact on the third year pupils who have chosen to study a language at national level.
In Inverclyde schools, modern languages are optional from third year onwards.
Many of the pupils listening to the talk said afterwards that, like Anna, they want to travel.
Among them Anna Nelis told the Tele: "I love Spanish and I really want to travel. I was really impressed listening to Anna."
Modern languages principal Ms Donnelly said: "It was wonderful to have Anna here. She is incredible and has taken every opportunity. Anna is the perfect example of what you can achieve with languages.
"I heard some of the pupils saying that they were re-evaluating their lives following her talk."

item.title: [The Mercury News] Dear Abby: My co-workers smirk and stare because of my failed romance
item.dc:creator: Abigail Van Buren
item.description: DEAR ABBY: I am a man in my 40s. A woman and I had a relationship that ended badly. We met on the job. Everyone at work knows about our former relationship, and it is extremely awkward, though we are in different departments. Every time I walk by, there are lots of smiles and chattering; when I approach my co-workers’ desks, I’m greeted with silence and intense stares. I still have strong feelings for her, and I know they are reciprocated because she has verbalized it and shown it with her actio
item.content:encoded:
DEAR ABBY: I am a man in my 40s. A woman and I had a relationship that ended badly. We met on the job.
Everyone at work knows about our former relationship, and it is extremely awkward, though we are in different departments. Every time I walk by, there are lots of smiles and chattering; when I approach my co-workers’ desks, I’m greeted with silence and intense stares.
I still have strong feelings for her, and I know they are reciprocated because she has verbalized it and shown it with her actions and behaviors.
After she ended things, I was upset and gave her the silent treatment. I know she feels hurt by my pretending like she doesn’t exist. I am a stubborn man, but I really miss her.
After the breakup, she mentioned being friends. I cannot be friends with her.
Despite the amount of time that has gone by, I still want to fix things. However, I know my real intentions and illusions about getting back together are misguided fantasy. I would appreciate your insights.
— AWKWARD AT WORK
DEAR AWKWARD: Do you understand that it’s you, not your co-workers, making things awkward? By resorting to the silent treatment, you’ve made everyone uncomfortable.
You say you want to fix things, but you’ve made no attempt to do so. You don’t believe you can reconcile with your ex, but on what grounds? You won’t even talk to her!
I don’t think you’re “stubborn”; I think you’re afraid. You’ve kept up this unseemly behavior because you don’t want to be hurt again.
If you can’t muster the courage to tell this woman you want another chance, you have two options left: Either speak with her purely as a colleague and bury the hatchet so you can at least be cordial in the workplace, or start looking for another job.
DEAR ABBY: My father’s girlfriend, “Jane,” has started soliciting money for her causes from everyone she knows, especially our family members.
After the first request, I donated a modest amount to support her, not knowing the deluge of requests that would follow. I have a set amount of money I can use for charity and would rather decide for myself how to spend it.
Jane and my father are sensitive about her being accepted into our family. They both tend to look for slights and then blow them out of proportion. Dad has made it clear that unless my siblings and I fully embrace Jane, he won’t be part of our lives.
I admire him sticking up for her, but I know if I decline the next donation request it’s going to get ugly. I feel like I’m being held hostage. How do I get out of this situation?
— HELD HOSTAGE IN VANCOUVER
DEAR HELD HOSTAGE: Talk to your father privately and tell him you love him. Remind him that you don’t have an unlimited amount of money to donate to charity, that you have causes of your own that are important to you, and that you have already donated to Jane’s more than once. Ask him to explain that to her and that it isn’t a rejection of her — just fiscal responsibility on your part.
He needs to know you feel like you won’t be able to have a relationship with the father you adore if you refuse these solicitations.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips wrote this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

item.title: [The Guardian] Blind date: ‘We talked about how I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?’
item.dc:creator: Guardian Staff; Guardian staff reporter
item.description: Dec on Dave What were you hoping for? A sweet-hearted madman who would make me belly laugh. First impressions? Looked like a David. A bit nervous and jittery, but considerate, curious and chatty (all the best C-words). What did you talk about? People in cars shouting “ginge” at him. Us coming from the West Country (but only I sound like it). How I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives? Most awkward moment? I tried on his stethoscope, pretending to listen for a heartbeat from the chi
item.content:encoded:
Dec on Dave
What were you hoping for?
A sweet-hearted madman who would make me belly laugh.
First impressions?
Looked like a David. A bit nervous and jittery, but considerate, curious and chatty (all the best C-words).
What did you talk about?
People in cars shouting “ginge” at him. Us coming from the West Country (but only I sound like it). How I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?
Most awkward moment?
I tried on his stethoscope, pretending to listen for a heartbeat from the chicken.
Good table manners?
Sound as a pound.
Best thing about David?
His passion for his profession. Also, how he was so keen to ask, listen and hear.
Would you introduce David to your friends?
Possibly, so they can give him his second Buzzballz ever!
Describe David in three words
Moustached, kind, grounded.
What do you think David made of you?
Probably an absolute loony. No, I wonder if he saw through the tarty humour to my kind, smart, caring self.
Did you go on somewhere?
The kitchen was closing, and he had to work in the morning, saving lives – very inconsiderate.
And … did you kiss?
I gave him a polite peck on the cheek when we hugged bye-bye.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
Nothing: it was the perfect balance of sincere connection and nonsense.
Marks out of 10?
A solid 6. He’s a cracking bloke and rocks a floral shirt better than anyone I know. It’s a 6 not a 7 because I don’t like fish or salad; he kindly ordered me both.
Would you meet again?
We swapped numbers. We’re not each other’s “spark”, but had a good evening.
David on Dec
What were you hoping for?
Someone who put me at ease, asked me questions and made me want to text my friends about him in the toilet.
First impressions?
Definitely a main character. Handsome, potty-mouthed, charming and equally clueless about tapas.
What did you talk about?
Dec’s love of swearing. Coming out.
Most awkward moment?
Possibly when I realised I had a child’s blood on my trousers.
Good table manners?
Impeccable.
Best thing about Dec?
He’s very free and at ease in himself, and made me feel I could be too. And his autobiography will be a bestseller.
Would you introduce Dec to your friends?
I would. But I didn’t toilet-text them.
Describe Dec in three words
Curious, beautiful, free.
What do you think Dec made of you?
Hopefully good company! “Doctor” brings a whole set of expectations, but it felt like he was able to see past all that.
Did you go on somewhere?
We didn’t – but we stayed until closing.
And … did you kiss?
A quick peck at the station.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
We were side-by-side at the bar, which is weird for a first date. And he got my right side, which is definitely less good.
Marks out of 10?
8.
Would you meet again?
We agreed the chemistry felt more friendly than romantic, but I’d love to stay in touch.
Dec and David ate at Barrafina Drury Lane, London WC2. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

Both concern being present and connected each day. That matters beyond the wedding. Long-term relationships can falter when practical conversations replace emotional ones. item.content:encoded:
Column by Penny Newton-Hurley
DUA Lipa recently shared her wedding advice: experience the day as a guest would and stay close to your husband.
Both concern being present and connected each day.
That matters beyond the wedding.
Long-term relationships can falter when practical conversations replace emotional ones.
We talk about school runs, shopping, bills and appointments, but stop asking: “How are you, really?”
When a partner says, “You’re never here,” the words may sound accusing.
Underneath them might be loneliness and a longing for closeness.
The listener hears criticism and replies defensively: “I’m working to support us.”
Now both people are protecting themselves and neither feels understood.
Try slowing the exchange down.
Separate the fact from the judgement, identify the feeling and consider what is needed.
“I’ve noticed we haven’t spent an evening together this week. I miss you and would love time to reconnect. Could we keep Friday evening free?”
This does not guarantee the answer will be yes.
But it makes connection more likely than blame does.
This approach is part of the four-stage MECAnism in my book, The Human Language, out now.
It helps us recognise our thoughts, emotions and core needs before deciding what to say or do.
Staying close on a wedding day is lovely advice.
Staying curious, emotionally honest and connected throughout the days that follow is what sustains a relationship.
The photographs may capture the celebration, but it is the quieter conversations afterwards that build a marriage.
Penny Newton-Hurley is an Oakridge-based communication consultant and mediator.
Her new book, The Human Language, is out now, priced £12.99, and available from bookshops and Amazon.

item.content:encoded:
I’ve just tried blind speed-dating. Missed it in my twenties. Was too square.
Now in a spasm of late forties’ angst I’ve spent hours calling total strangers trying to make them like me.
I didn’t ever think I’d end up speed-dating. Didn’t think the wife would approve – or that would-be girl for that matter. I’m a bit out of practice – and out of shape let’s face it. But after this week, like a 49-year-old virgin on a first date, I’ve become something of a silver-tongued suitor. Just not on the right people. I’m told girls love questions. It shows you care. But I’ve discovered that civil servants on the end of a phone don’t. Even if they’re called Shahida.
My wife Tetiana needed a share code. It’s an electronic ID. A random mix of numbers and letters the government gives you if you’re not a citizen so you can work, rent or, in our case, get a mortgage. They should just tattoo it on your arm when you first arrive at Dover. There’s an idea Nigel.
Now, Tetiana has been in the country since 2009. She has Indefinite Leave to Remain. Stamped in her passport – two passports ago. She’s allowed in even though in her fur coat she looks like a Romanian people smuggler. She can be let loose on a mental health clinic but she can’t vote. Then three months into the remortgaging process, our mortgage advisor suddenly tells us they don’t accept paper visas. Although they did five years ago. You need a share code.
How do you get a share code? First, you set up a UKVI – UK Visas and Immigration – online account. Then they make you shlep all the way to Croydon to give your biometrics. It’s deliberate. If the office was in Hove, no one would ever leave the country. But who would want to stay in the UK after going to Croydon? In reality, most people who go to Croydon for a visa never actually leave. Because, trouble is, once Rick Deckard has bagged up your blood, hair, toenail clippings and fingerprints, you’re in no fit state to go anywhere else. So that’s Croydon.
And then you wait. And wait. Now a mortgage has a deadline. If you think you’re clobbered by your interest rate now, wait till you go on the standard variable rate. We had until September 23. Where was our share code? Silly me. Who’s going to catch any Home Office civil servant worth their salt working in August? Or even in England. I started to look up by-elections in Scotland to help make ends meet.
So, deep breath, we decide to phone UKVI. This is where speed dating skills come in handy. If Ovid was alive today, he wouldn’t write about the Minotaur – that horned cow at the centre of a labyrinth. No. He’d write about UKVI phone options. Because before you get to impress anyone with your wit, you need to press number 4. Then number 2. Then number 4. Then number 4 again. Then number 2. There are more numbers called out than during a night at Mecca bingo. Advisors are more protected from foreign reach than our gold bullion under Threadneedle Street.
It wouldn’t be so bad if it wasn’t a different advisor each time. “Calls may be recorded for training and data protection purposes.” Not to actually relieve you from having to tell them your problem all over again each time. And that’s before you’ve got past security. How long is your inside leg? What’s your cat’s middle name? Someone suddenly speaks: “How can I help you?” Can I remember how to speak English? “My wife needs a share code.” I hope he can smell my aftershave. Can pheromones travel down the phone line? “Have you got a UKVI account?” “Yes.” “Hang on a minute.”
Something in his voice told me this potential lover would never find my wife’s electronic data. My wife and I decide to tag team. The music stops and it’s time to move on. By the end of the night, no one’s marked my score card. Not even the wife.
All I can say is Tetiana must have more experience kissing frogs than me. However she wooed him, it worked. She probably chanced upon someone on day release from some luxury hotel that provides all day breakfast. With the speed and grace of a concierge at the Ritz, it took this marvel of productivity fewer than five minutes to fix my wife’s share code.
You can order swarms of bees on Amazon but if the state loses your data, it’s like looking for a yellow Lego brick in a children’s sand pit. Pity help us when the replicants take over.
Alistair McNair is Leader of the Conservatives on Brighton and Hove City Council.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Saturday, September 19: Feelings Change Today
Your zodiac sign's love horoscope is here for September 19, 2026. Venus in Libra aligns with retrograde Uranus in Gemini on Saturday, changing your feelings in a way you probably didn't see coming.
This doesn’t necessarily mean your relationship will experience difficulties, but you should hold space for an outcome you didn't expect. Let your feelings change and surprise you, as that's the best way to end up with the person meant for you.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Saturday, September 19, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Give this connection a chance, Aries. September 19 brings an intense moment, challenging you to be flexible. You may find yourself completely changing directions or having a conversation you thought you’d already made peace with.
You find out the truth of how someone feels towards you, and you will also have to decide how honest you want to be with them in return. Just know that if you hold anything back during Saturday's love horoscope, it will eventually come out.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Lean into what feels right, Taurus, and honor what and who is most important to you in your life. Your love horoscope today offers you an opportunity to break free from a bad pattern.
No matter what it may bring to your life, choosing what feels right for you is crucial. Saturday brings you the chance to grow and finally start moving towards your destiny.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It’s OK if your feelings change, Gemini. As an air sign that carries a sense of duality, you are no stranger to changing your mind. However, changing your mind about your job is different than your love life.
Still, that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t honor those more personal changes. On Saturday, you're becoming aware that your feelings have changed, and it is in your best interest to honor that new truth.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Take some quiet time for yourself on Saturday, Cancer. It’s OK to cancel plans or honor the boundaries for what you need.
Before you make any decisions or promises in your love life, you must be sure that actually moving in ways your future self will thank you for. There is a chance that what you’re doing is more about your inner wounds than a new pattern. September 19 offers you the chance to correct your path.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Listen to your inner self, Leo. You may feel like there is a lot of noise around you on Saturday. Everyone has an opinion about what you should do in your life. While your friends and family have good intentions, that doesn’t mean you should let them direct your choices.
Focus on what you actually know to be true and how certain relationships feel for you. This is a time to listen to your inner self over the opinions of others.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This is the change you need, Virgo. You have made plans and found comfort in thinking that you know what to expect from the future. However, someone comes into your life on Saturday who makes you question everything.
This person brings a divine opportunity for change. You may wonder if this new offer is too good to be true, but you can trust it will change your life in the best way.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Let yourself choose what and who truly resonates with your soul, Libra. On Saturday, you are being guided toward a new path in your life. This isn’t only about romance, but also about where you live and the work you do.
This will take you far from your comfort zone, but it is also deeply connected to your fate. Stay aware of the offers and people that arrive in your life now and in the coming days. Just because you didn’t plan for any of this doesn’t mean it’s not meant for you.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your heart is never wrong, Scorpio, so take a moment during Saturday's love horoscope to really listen to it. You crave a deep and meaningful relationship, yet you’ve allowed yourself to accept far less. Well, no more.
Hold space for the healing this new path will require. Know that to get that amazing, deep love you desire, you must also let yourself grow into the person who can handle it.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You’re not meant to talk yourself out of love, Sagittarius. The person meant for you is rarely the most convenient or easy option. This is because the greatest love often requires the greatest risk.
As of September 19, you can no longer talk yourself out of taking this chance. Everything inside you is ready to see what this connection actually is. You can take your time, but you can’t ignore how you feel any longer.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Make space for new and fresh energy, Capricorn. On Saturday, don’t be afraid to say yes to change or to shifting your life in new and exciting ways.
You have love around you, but it's time to shake up your routine and find the life that feels good to your soul. By embracing change and becoming more spontaneous, you will also be able to hold space for someone in your life when they finally confess to you how they feel.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Love always changes your life, Aquarius. As much as you crave adventure and excitement, you prefer to be the one who changes your own life. But letting love bring in new opportunities doesn’t mean you’re giving up your power.
Every choice you’ve made has led you to this very moment. Now, you need to let love direct your next steps. Don’t be afraid to surprise even yourself with the choices you make.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
When it’s right, you will know, Pisces. As much as you plan to take your time and progress a relationship slowly, you must remain flexible. This doesn’t mean rushing anything or jumping into a new karmic connection, but you must stay open-minded.
A connection in your life is progressing more quickly than you planned. In your heart, you know it’s right, so let yourself see where this love goes, even if the pace is different from what you expected.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.title: [E! News] Malcolm in the Middle’s Frankie Muniz Details Hitting “Rock Bottom” Weeks After Divorce News
item.dc:creator: Sabba Rahbar
item.description: Frankie Muniz isn’t racing away from his struggles. The Malcolm in the Middle actor got candid about what he’s been going through over the last six weeks, admitting his life has felt like “a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from.” “Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time,” Muniz posted on X Sept. 18. “I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone.” The admission comes over two months after he and wife Paige Price—with whom he shares 5-year-old son Mauz Mosley Muniz
item.content:encoded:
Frankie Muniz isn’t racing away from his struggles.
The Malcolm in the Middle actor got candid about what he’s been going through over the last six weeks, admitting his life has felt like “a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from.”
“Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time,” Muniz posted on X Sept. 18. “I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone.”
The admission comes over two months after he and wife Paige Price—with whom he shares 5-year-old son Mauz Mosley Muniz—announced their divorce after six years of marriage.
Still, there is a silver lining for the 40-year-old, as he explained, “The unexpected gift in the middle of it is that I’ve had nowhere to hide. I’ve had time to sit with myself, do real self-reflection, and finally see the areas of my life that need work if I want to become a better version of me. Not the polished version I show the world...the actual one.”
Muniz said he recently read that "sometimes hitting rock bottom is the thing that wakes you up" and becomes a catalyst to force “the changes you needed to make all along so you can live the best life possible.”
And that idea stayed with the race car driver, who imagined in five years time he will “look back at this exact low point and feel grateful for it,” especially because getting to a better place in his life necessitated going through the difficulty.
“This isn’t the end of the story. It’s the part where I start doing the work...the uncomfortable, unglamorous, necessary work. I’m choosing to treat this season as the foundation, not the finish line,” Muniz wrote. “If you’re in a low place right now too, you’re not broken. You’re being rebuilt. Let's keep going!”
In recent weeks, Muniz has been open about the difficult time he’s been facing, posting on X Aug. 26, “Am I naive to say that I didn't know that having a broken heart actually meant your heart physically aches. I'd rather break my back again.”
On Sept. 1 he wrote, “Struggling,” and a few days later on Sept. 6 shared two photos of himself as a child, captioning the pictures, “Sometimes I wish I could go back to this.”
For more stars who have been candid about their own struggles, keep reading.

item.content:encoded:
As streamers go, Netflix has one of the very best collections of original romance movies. The streaming platform is the home of modern romance classics like Set It Up, the To All the Boys I've Loved Before trilogy, The Wrong Paris, and People We Meet on Vacation. Netflix's romance movies are known for having well-written characters that are easy to get attached to, as well as compelling dynamics and strong chemistry between these characters.
While Netflix has a number of romance movies that are pretty much universally beloved, it also has some truly excellent ones that have slipped through the cracks over the years. These movies have clever main premises, strong dialogue, and captivating romances. These are forgotten Netflix romance movies that are truly perfect from start to finish.
'Along for the Ride' (2022)
Based on the Sarah Dessen novel of the same name, Along for the Ride follows a recent high school graduate named Auden (Emma Pasarow) who goes to stay at her father's home in a beach town called Colby, North Carolina for the summer. Auden is very ambitious and academic-minded, so she's missed out on most normal teenage experiences. Auden is already starting at her dream college in the fall, so now, she has the summer off to catch up on some of the things that she has missed out on.
Very quickly, Auden gets a job, makes some friends, and starts spending her nights going on mini-adventures with fellow insomniac Eli (Belmont Cameli). Auden's father (Dermot Mulroney) is more interested in writing his latest novel than parenting either her or his newborn baby, and Auden doesn't know how to connect with his wife (Kate Bosworth), so she spends more time out and about than at home. As Eli helps her check off items on the list of things she missed, the two start to really get to know each other. Auden and Eli's nights together are a bubble away from the more difficult things in their lives, though, and they soon realize that these outside obstacles could threaten their new connection. Along for the Ride is a sweet and cozy summer romance, and it remains severely underrated four years after it was released.
'Someone Great' (2019)
Someone Great is a beautiful movie with a romance that takes place out of order. Music journalist Jenny (Gina Rodriguez) is preparing to move from New York City to San Francisco for her dream job, and her boyfriend of nine years, Nate (Lakeith Stanfield), has just broken up with her. Thus, Jenny's two best friends, Blair (Brittany Snow) and Erin (DeWanda Wise), decide to cheer Jenny up and send her off by all having one last big adventure together before she moves.
Over the course of one life-changing day, Jenny, Blair, and Erin all reevaluate their paths and love lives. For Jenny, this means looking back on her memories with Nate and trying to determine where it all went wrong. For Blair, this means attempting to finally break up with Will (Alex Moffat), her boyfriend with whom she's no longer in love. Erin, meanwhile, has found a real connection with her new girlfriend, Leah (Rebecca Naomi Jones), but she is afraid to actually commit to her. Someone Great is an excellent movie that divides its romantic storylines amongst its three leads, taking them each on a journey to determine whether they want to fight for their relationships.
'Candy Jar' (2018)
Candy Jar is a coming-of-age romantic comedy about two high school debate team rivals, Lona (Sami Gayle) and Bennet (Jacob Latimore). They are the only two members of their school's debate club, and they are competing to become the club's president in order to look good to colleges. When they are reluctantly made co-presidents, Lona and Bennet start spending more time together, and they begin to question their previous impressions of each other.
Candy Jar is a funny and sweet rivals-to-lovers movie that is perfect for romance fans. Lona and Bennet are the only people who really understand each other, but their similarities also act as an obstacle to their romance. Both of their mothers put pressure on them to be the best no matter what, and they both worry about the potential risks that compromising and setting their rivalry aside could have on their futures.
'Love at First Sight' (2023)
Based on the novel The Statistical Probability of Love at First Sight by Jennifer E. Smith, Love at First Sight follows two college students who meet at JFK airport while preparing to board a flight to London. Hadley (Haley Lu Richardson) is on her way to the second wedding of her father, whom she still resents for moving away so quickly after his divorce from her mother. Oliver (Ben Hardy) is going home for a family event, although he's vague with her about the specifics. Hadley and Oliver immediately strike a connection, and they get to know each other better on the plane.
When a technological mishap prevents Hadley from saving Oliver's number after the flight, they're separated, and she is determined to find her way back to him. Oliver, meanwhile, unknowingly waits to hear from her. Love at First Sight is a really sweet and emotional movie that questions the possibility of the concept of love at first sight through the story of Hadley and Oliver. The two barely know each other, but they both take a number of risks and bold swings in order to fight for the possibility of their romance.
'Wedding Season' (2022)
Wedding Season is a fantastic fake-dating romantic comedy that follows Asha (Pallavi Sharda), a woman who recently both ended her engagement and left her face-paced job on Wall Street to work for a New Jersey-based startup. When Asha's mother pressures her to set up an online dating profile, she meets Ravi (Suraj Sharma), but their date doesn't go well. After the two cross paths at a wedding, though, Asha asks Ravi to fake a relationship with her for the remainder of the weddings that they both have to attend that summer.
Thus, Asha and Ravi go to the rest of the weddings together that summer, pretending to be a couple so that their families no longer put pressure on them. Asha, in particular, isn't looking for love, and is much more determined to prove herself at work. Still, though, she and Ravi start to really start to form a connection through their fake relationship. The only problem is, there is a ticking clock on their fake romance, and Asha starts to realize that she might not be ready for it to end. Wedding Season is such a fun and swoonworthy rom-com, and romance fans who love wedding movies will really enjoy this one.
'The Lovebirds' (2020)
The Love Birds is an action rom-com that starts with a breakup. Leilani (Issa Rae) and Jibran (Kumail Nanjiani) once had the perfect romance. Now, though, it's been four years, and they fight all the time. Finally, on the way to a dinner party, Jibran and Leilani decide to break up. Seconds later, though, they hit a cyclist with their car. The cyclist then refuses their help, and another man steps in and kills him with their car, pulling a confused Leilani and Jibrani into a dangerous conspiracy.
Worried that they will be blamed for the man's death, Leilani and Jibran decide to pursue the conspiracy and solve his murder. The more entangled the former couple gets in this investigation, though, the more danger they find themselves in. The Lovebirds is an absolutely hilarious movie with a compelling action plot and an excellent second chance romance, where Leilani and Jibran start to see each other in a new light thanks to the life-and-death stakes at play.
'The Half of It' (2020)
The Half of It is a Cyrano de Bergerac-inspired coming-of-age movie about a teenage girl named Ellie Chu (Leah Lewis). Ellie lives in a small town called Squahamish, and since the death of her mother years earlier, she helps her father support the two of them by writing her classmates' essays for money. One day, Ellie's neighbor, Paul Munsky (Daniel Diemer), offers to pay her to write a love letter to his crush, the popular Aster Flores (Alexxis Lemire). Despite her own secret crush on Aster, Ellie agrees to it, but the letter quickly spirals into constant texting.
The Half of It has everything: a beautiful coming-of-age story, a lovely and unexpected friendship between Ellie and Paul, and a complicated love square involving the two of them, Aster, and her boyfriend. The romance between Ellie and Aster develops completely through writing, with Ellie feeling conflicted over the lie that brought them together in the first place. Meanwhile, Aster believes that Paul is the one that she is falling for.

Singles can change their previous tastes. Couples can resolve an issue which has been neglected for far too long. How to Navigate Today’s Energy Instead of reacting to the latest event, look at the root cause of any romantic worry. Mula can expose what has been eating away at trust or interest in silence. This is good f
item.content:encoded:
An increased desire to understand the real nature of a relationship, as well as emotional cleansing and honesty. Mula Nakshatra encourages people to see the depths of attraction. Singles can change their previous tastes. Couples can resolve an issue which has been neglected for far too long.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
Instead of reacting to the latest event, look at the root cause of any romantic worry. Mula can expose what has been eating away at trust or interest in silence. This is good for disambiguation but may be harmful when the language is harsh. Couples should talk about patterns rather than blame a single incident. Singles might wonder if a new spark is based on real compatibility or just excitement. Compassion is the best way to deliver truth.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Gemini: Your relationship may seem more unpredictable than usual. Never change your position every time the mood changes. Give yourself plenty of time to discover what you really want before you answer.
Virgo: The whole bond should not be called into question because of a single imperfect habit.
Determine if the problem is significant or just an annoyance.
Pisces might want to be independent, but emotional expectations could get in the way. Don’t see freedom as a free pass for indifference. Setting clear boundaries and realistic expectations can help in avoiding disappointment.
Taurus romance can be affected by a financial, family or trust matter. Don’t combine multiple issues into one argument.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Sagittarius: Your frankness may appeal to someone who appreciates direct communication. Singles can also connect based on shared values, travel, education or an unconventional social setting. Couples may enjoy trying something totally new together.
Aries: Bold romantic action can get things moving. You might find a person responds positively when you show real interest, and stop waiting for the perfect conditions.
Leo: Your confidence can make you more conspicuous. A social plan, a trip or even a little bit of banter can take chemistry up a notch and add some warmth to an existing bond.
Aquarius: Seeing someone from a new perspective can change how you relate to them. This can create a deeper, more emotional connection, especially if you both prize freedom and honesty.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Cancer: Intense emotions are enabling you to be patient with decisions.
Libra: Balancing difficult facts could be good for a relationship.
Scorpio:
Still very attracted, but control might cause resistance.
Capricorn:
Love is stable, but not necessarily practical.
Lucky Action of the Day
Get rid of one old-fashioned assumption you have about someone you admire. See the person as they are in the present, not as you once knew them.

item.title: [Discover SWNS] These subtle behaviors could be signs of 'micro-cheating,' therapist says - Discover SWNS
item.dc:creator: Lauren Wilkin
item.description: A couples therapist has revealed the subtle behaviors that could be signs of “micro-cheating” – from deleting messages to suddenly becoming protective of your phone. Dr. Anna Elton, a licensed marriage and family therapist, says micro-cheating and boundary-crossing are common sources of relationship problems in her practice. item.content:encoded:
A couples therapist has revealed the subtle behaviors that could be signs of “micro-cheating” – from deleting messages to suddenly becoming protective of your phone.
Dr. Anna Elton, a licensed marriage and family therapist, says micro-cheating and boundary-crossing are common sources of relationship problems in her practice.
But she says liking someone’s photo, messaging an ex or becoming more private with your phone isn’t automatically evidence of cheating.
Instead, she says the biggest things to consider are intent, secrecy and whether romantic or sexual attention is being directed outside the relationship.
Dr. Elton, from West Palm Beach, Florida, said: “I think of micro-cheating as a pattern of seemingly small behaviours in which a person’s romantic or sexual attention and desire begin to move outside the relationship in ways that violate the boundaries the couple has established.
“The behaviour itself may look small, but the intention behind it can tell you much more about whether a boundary is being crossed.
“Intent matters.
“Liking someone’s photo, sending a message, or talking to an ex is not automatically micro-cheating.”
Dr. Elton says people questioning their own behavior should consider what they are hoping to get from the interaction.
She said: “Ask yourself: Why are you doing it? Are you simply interacting, or are you looking for attention, validation, excitement, or connection that you are not getting in your relationship?
“Examples could include repeatedly liking or commenting on someone’s suggestive photos because you are attracted to them, initiating contact with someone you have romantic or sexual interest in, sending flirtatious messages.”
Dr. Elton, author of “Couples Therapy in the Digital Age,” said secretly maintaining contact with an ex or seeking romantic validation from someone outside a relationship could also cross a boundary.
She said: “One isolated action may seem insignificant, but acts of micro-cheating can begin to pile up, potentially revealing a larger pattern of secrecy and boundary-crossing.
“Couples also frequently tell me, ‘but we never actually discussed whether this was a boundary’. That is very common.
“Most couples do not sit down at the beginning of a relationship and create a detailed rulebook for every possible interaction.
“In those situations, ask yourself: If my partner knew exactly what I was doing, would they likely feel hurt or disrespected? If the answer is yes, that is probably a conversation worth having.”
Dr. Elton also cautioned against assuming that changes in someone’s phone or social media habits mean they are being unfaithful.
She said: “I would caution people against treating any single behaviour as proof of micro-cheating. Changes in phone use, privacy, or social media habits can have many explanations.
“What matters more is whether those changes are part of a larger pattern of secrecy or redirected romantic or sexual attention.
“Another sign can be a shift in emotional energy.
“Someone may become unusually excited about communicating with another person while simultaneously becoming less engaged or affectionate with their partner.”
Dr. Elton says there is also an important distinction between privacy and secrecy.
She said: “Everyone is entitled to privacy within a relationship.
“Secrecy is different.
“Privacy says, ‘this is something that belongs to me’. Secrecy often says, ‘I need to make sure my partner does not know about this because I know it could affect our relationship’.”
In her experience, Dr. Elton says deleting messages, hiding communication, minimizing a connection or lying about who you are talking to can warrant a conversation.
She said micro-cheating does not necessarily lead to physical infidelity, but can still damage a relationship.
“I would be careful about assuming that it will, but it can still damage a relationship on its own,” she said.
“The impact comes from the gradual redirection of attention, curiosity, emotional energy, or desire away from the primary relationship.
“A partner may begin investing excitement and anticipation in someone else while becoming less emotionally available at home.
“These behaviours can also create an accumulation of small breaches of trust.”
Dr. Elton, who has 15 years of experience as a clinical sexologist, added: “For many couples, the most painful part is discovering that their partner understood the behaviour might hurt them and chose to hide it anyway.”
She says couples can reduce the risk of crossing boundaries by discussing what they consider acceptable.
Dr. Elton suggests dividing a piece of paper into three columns – acceptable behaviors, unacceptable behaviors and a “gray area.”
She said: “These are the behaviours you are not completely sure about, such as messaging an ex, liking suggestive photos, private conversations with someone you are attracted to, or maintaining certain friendships online.
“Partners can do this separately and then compare notes, or complete it together as a couple.”
Dr. Elton says the exercise can reveal that couples who assumed they shared the same boundaries actually have very different ideas about what is acceptable.
Discussing those differences can help couples establish clearer boundaries in the future.

item.content:encoded:
HBO and Sky Television's upcoming legal drama, War, starring Dominic West and Sienna Miller, will be released on October 1 and 2, respectively. Created by George Kay, this legal series will follow the lives of London's most powerful lawyers from firms Taylor & Byrne and Cathcarts & Sons as they clash over a pivotal legal battle. Season 1 will follow the divorce of British tech entrepreneur Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) and film star Carla Duval (Sienna Miller) as the legal firms race to secure victory for their respective clients.
At the London premiere of their upcoming legal drama, Sienna Miller and Dominic West weighed in on divorce. Speaking to the Associated Press on whether people would think of getting a divorce after watching War, Miller said,
"They might rethink a divorce."
West added that the series does not recommend couples getting a divorce. He advised couples to resolve differences outside the court. While the reporter asked whether living in different countries would help, West said that it was a great idea.
Here's more about it.
War London premiere: Sienna Miller says prenups defeat the purpose of marriage
At the London premiere, Miller said that prenups defeat the purpose of a marriage. She told the Press Association (via The Standard):
"I feel like it kind of defeats the purpose of going into a marriage and making that commitment. But I also understand."
The series is set to explore how prenups are usually not legally binding or enforceable by courts in Wales and England. West called it a waste of time. West added that he loves legal dramas and, most importantly, the twists and turns they contain.
Advertisement
War: Release date, cast, and more about the upcoming HBO legal drama
War was initially announced in 2025 when HBO teamed up with Sky for two seasons. Currently, Season 2 is in production, and Marisa Tomei, David Harewood, and Kelly Macdonald will guest star in Season 2.
War Season 1 will premiere on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 9 PM ET on HBO. Apart from Miller and West, Season 1 stars Phoebe Fox as Serena Byrne, James McArdle as Nicholas Taylor, Nina Sosanya as "Her Majesty" Beatrice "Queen Bea" Ubosi, and Pip Torrens as John Smallwood. It also features Archie Renaux as Jonathan "Johnny" Warren.
Season 1 will also be available in Italy, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Australia, Austria, France, Asia, and Belgium. NBCUniversal Global TV Distribution is responsible for the global sales. It is produced by New Pictures, a Banijay Company, and Observatory Pictures, in association with Sky and HBO.
Speaking to Variety, Kay, who also serves as the writer and executive producer of the series, said that he was eager to go to a mainstream TV show. He added that he had previously worked on thrillers and crime shows, but now he is eager to do character-driven, high-end shows.
"I was thinking about doing this legal show because I love the idea that a case that you’re working on as a lawyer is a kind of metaphor for your own life, where you’re constantly bringing the personal into the professional."
Speaking about War, he added that it is about two high-end rival London law firms. He explained he wanted to do one traditional and older firm and another fresh, ambitious firm with fewer resources but full of smart characters.
"No one’s dusty, but there’s the traditional one, and there’s the modern one. Each season we can come back and reboot with guest star clients."
Follow SoapCentral for more such updates.

item.title: [ELLE India] Two Weeks Is Enough To Spot These Relationship Red Flags
item.dc:creator: Madiha Siddiqui
item.description: 14 Days, A Few Dates, And The Red Flags You Need To Notice A Two-Week window cannot tell you everything about someone. But a few dates can reveal early red flags in how they communicate, respect you and handle getting closer. Two Weeks Can Reveal Early Red Flags You are not looking for perfection this early. You are noticing patterns: inconsistency, pressure, dismissiveness or whether their words and actions already seem to be telling two different stories. Intensity Isn’t Always Intimacy Consta
item.content:encoded:
14 Days, A Few Dates, And The Red Flags You Need To Notice
A Two-Week window cannot tell you everything about someone. But a few dates can reveal early red flags in how they communicate, respect you and handle getting closer.
Two Weeks Can Reveal Early Red Flags
You are not looking for perfection this early. You are noticing patterns: inconsistency, pressure, dismissiveness or whether their words and actions already seem to be telling two different stories.
Intensity Isn’t Always Intimacy
Constant texts, huge declarations and talking about a future together after three dates can feel flattering. Love bombing becomes a concern when intensity starts replacing genuine trust and time.
Watch How They Handle Your Boundaries
The real test is not whether they like your boundaries, but whether they respect them. Turning up unannounced, pushing for more time or making “no” feel negotiable deserves attention.
Delayed Replies Shouldn’t Become A Problem
Healthy communication does not mean texting every five minutes. But guilt-tripping you over a late reply, demanding constant updates or treating access to you like an entitlement is different.
Pay Attention To The “Jokes”
A joke stops being harmless when you are always the punchline. Little digs about your clothes, friends, work or appearance can reveal disrespect long before anyone calls it that.
Your Body Can Notice Before You Do
Sometimes the first sign is less obvious: you feel tense before meeting them, rehearse what to say or leave dates strangely drained. That discomfort is worth noticing, not immediately explaining away.
Two Weeks Cannot Predict Compatibility
Chemistry can arrive quickly. Compatibility usually takes longer. Shared values, conflict styles, ambitions and how someone behaves once the novelty fades cannot really be rushed into 14 days.
Notice Patterns Before You Explain Them Away
One awkward moment is human. Repeated behaviour is information. Early red flags matter less as isolated incidents and more when you keep finding yourself making excuses for the same thing.

item.content:encoded:
Dating apps were already hard enough.
Now imagine spending weeks flirting with someone, buying virtual coins just to keep talking to them and maybe even getting emotionally attached…
only to discover your situationship was basically ChatGPT with a profile picture.
Security researchers have uncovered a surprisingly sophisticated network of dating apps using AI-generated personas to convince users they were talking to real people.
Apps including Dora, Romi and Doni reportedly used thousands of fake personas capable of chatting around the clock, sending messages and keeping users engaged , while the apps encouraged them to spend money on virtual currency to continue conversations.
And this wasn’t some tiny operation.
Researchers identified more than 4,700 AI personas, interacting with around 25,000 users and sending 2.36 million messages in just two weeks.
The whole thing was apparently built like an actual tech company, with growth plans, payment systems and tools designed to help the apps pass app-store reviews.
So yes.
Catfishing has officially received a software update.
At this point, before falling in love online, apparently we also need to ask:
“Select all the traffic lights in this picture.”
